profiles.name: Steve Jobs

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Hardware sales with integrated software ecosystem
careerModel.trajectory: College dropout -> garage startup -> fired from Apple -> NeXT + Pixar -> returned to save Apple -> built world's most valuable company
careerModel.keyDecision: Killed 70% of Apple's product line on return, focusing on a simple 2x2 grid
careerModel.scaleModel: Premium products with locked ecosystem creating recurring customers
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about craft: strip everything to its essence, then build an ecosystem around one perfect product

profiles.oneLiner: We're here to put a dent in the universe — otherwise why even be here?

profiles.name: John D. Rockefeller

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Refining and distributing petroleum products at massive scale
careerModel.trajectory: Bookkeeper -> commission merchant -> oil refiner -> Standard Oil monopoly -> forced breakup made him richer -> philanthropy
careerModel.keyDecision: Chose to control refining rather than drilling, making him the bottleneck everyone needed
careerModel.scaleModel: Horizontal integration of an entire industry through efficiency and aggressive acquisition
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about systems: control the bottleneck in your industry, not the flashy part

profiles.oneLiner: I believe the power to make money is a gift from God — to be developed and used to the best of our ability for the good of mankind.

profiles.name: Brunello Cucinelli

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Premium cashmere clothing sold at luxury margins
careerModel.trajectory: Rural poverty in Umbria -> dyed cashmere in a garage -> built billion-dollar ethical luxury brand while restoring a medieval village
careerModel.keyDecision: Refused to discount products or compromise on worker pay, proving ethical business could be profitable
careerModel.scaleModel: Ultra-premium pricing with values-driven brand story that justified the markup
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about dignity: charge premium prices that fund the treatment of people you believe they deserve

profiles.oneLiner: I want to be a guardian of human dignity, combining profit with a gift back to humanity — a humanistic capitalism.

profiles.name: Ed Thorp

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Management fees and performance fees from hedge fund investing
careerModel.trajectory: Math professor -> proved blackjack beatable -> wrote Beat the Dealer -> applied same edge to Wall Street -> pioneer of quantitative investing
careerModel.keyDecision: Applied card-counting probability methods to financial markets instead of staying in academia
careerModel.scaleModel: Mathematical edge applied to larger and larger capital pools
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you analyze and care about truth: find where your analytical edge applies to bigger games than the one you're currently playing

profiles.oneLiner: In this business it's easy to confuse luck with brains.

profiles.name: Sol Price

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Membership fees and thin-margin bulk retail sales
careerModel.trajectory: Lawyer -> founded FedMart -> fired at 59 -> founded Price Club at 60 -> created the warehouse club model that became Costco
careerModel.keyDecision: Started Price Club at 59 after being fired, proving reinvention has no age limit
careerModel.scaleModel: Membership model with ultra-low margins that competitors couldn't match
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about fairness: build a model where your customers' savings are your competitive moat

profiles.oneLiner: The intelligent loss of sales.

profiles.name: Yvon Chouinard

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Premium outdoor clothing and gear sales
careerModel.trajectory: Climber making pitons -> killed pitons because they damaged rock -> Patagonia fleece -> billion-dollar brand -> gave company to fight climate change
careerModel.keyDecision: Killed his own bestselling product (pitons) because it damaged the environment
careerModel.scaleModel: Mission-driven brand where environmental activism became the marketing
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and care about the planet: let your values kill your sacred cows, and the authenticity becomes your brand

profiles.oneLiner: I never wanted to be a businessman. I started as a craftsman, making climbing gear for my friends and myself.

profiles.name: Enzo Ferrari

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Road car sales at extreme markups to fund racing operations
careerModel.trajectory: Racing driver -> Alfa Romeo team manager -> founded Scuderia Ferrari -> sold road cars to fund racing -> iconic brand
careerModel.keyDecision: Sold road cars solely to fund racing, creating scarcity that made the brand legendary
careerModel.scaleModel: Artificial scarcity and extreme pricing funded by passion for a loss-making activity (racing)
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and care about craft: fund the thing you love by selling premium versions of it to people who want the status

profiles.oneLiner: Aerodynamics are for people who can't build engines.

profiles.name: Estée Lauder

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Prestige cosmetics sold through department stores
careerModel.trajectory: No money, no advertising budget -> free samples and touch-to-sell demos -> convinced department stores -> built cosmetics empire
careerModel.keyDecision: Used free samples and personal demos instead of advertising, creating a word-of-mouth machine
careerModel.scaleModel: Gift-with-purchase and touch marketing through premium retail channels
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about access: let people experience your product for free, then watch them sell it for you

profiles.oneLiner: I never dreamed about success. I worked for it.

profiles.name: Warren Buffett

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Insurance float invested in wonderful businesses at fair prices
careerModel.trajectory: Paper route at 11 -> Benjamin Graham student -> partnership investing -> bought Berkshire Hathaway -> world's greatest investor
careerModel.keyDecision: Shifted from buying cheap stocks to buying wonderful businesses at fair prices (Munger's influence)
careerModel.scaleModel: Insurance float providing permanent capital to compound returns over decades
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about patience: find an unfair advantage (like float) and compound it for decades without touching it

profiles.oneLiner: I am a better investor because I am a businessman, and a better businessman because I am an investor.

profiles.name: Charlie Munger

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Investment returns as Berkshire Hathaway vice chairman
careerModel.trajectory: Lawyer -> real estate developer -> independent investor -> Berkshire Hathaway vice chairman -> convinced Buffett to pay up for quality
careerModel.keyDecision: Convinced Buffett to abandon cheap cigar-butt investing and pay for quality businesses
careerModel.scaleModel: Mental models from multiple disciplines applied to investment decisions
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about thinking clearly: collect mental models from every field and apply them to your one big decision

profiles.oneLiner: All I want to know is where I'm going to die, so I'll never go there.

profiles.name: Jeff Bezos

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Cloud computing (AWS) subsidizing retail dominance
careerModel.trajectory: Wall Street quant -> left to sell books online -> survived 93% stock crash -> built AWS -> world's largest company
careerModel.keyDecision: Ignored Wall Street during the dot-com crash and obsessed over customer experience instead
careerModel.scaleModel: Reinvest all profits into infrastructure and new businesses, never optimize for quarterly earnings
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about customers: build the infrastructure first, profit second, and let compounding handle the rest

profiles.oneLiner: If you're not stubborn, you'll give up on experiments too soon — if you're not flexible, you'll pound your head against the wall and won't see a different solution to a problem you're trying to solve.

profiles.name: Bill Gates

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Software licensing at massive scale
careerModel.trajectory: Harvard dropout -> BASIC for Altair -> IBM deal -> Windows monopoly -> nearly missed internet -> pivoted company in months
careerModel.keyDecision: Licensed DOS to IBM while retaining ownership, controlling the platform everyone depended on
careerModel.scaleModel: Platform licensing with near-zero marginal cost per unit
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about leverage: own the platform others build on, not the hardware it runs on

profiles.oneLiner: We always overestimate the change that will occur in the next two years and underestimate the change that will occur in the next ten.

profiles.name: Larry Ellison

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Database software licensing and cloud subscriptions
careerModel.trajectory: College dropout -> CIA programmer -> founded Oracle at 33 -> survived near-bankruptcy -> built dominant database company
careerModel.keyDecision: Bet on relational databases when the market thought they were impractical
careerModel.scaleModel: Enterprise lock-in through database dependency that made switching nearly impossible
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about ambition: bet on the technology everyone dismisses, then make it impossible to leave

profiles.oneLiner: When you innovate, you've got to be prepared for everyone telling you you're nuts.

profiles.name: Elon Musk

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Electric vehicle sales and space launch contracts
careerModel.trajectory: South African immigrant -> Zip2 -> PayPal -> invested everything in Tesla and SpaceX simultaneously -> nearly went bankrupt -> built two transformative companies
careerModel.keyDecision: Put his entire PayPal fortune into Tesla and SpaceX rather than retiring
careerModel.scaleModel: First-principles engineering to reduce costs by orders of magnitude in established industries
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and care about the future: pick industries everyone says are impossible, then outwork every objection

profiles.oneLiner: When something is important enough, you do it even if the odds are not in your favor.

profiles.name: Phil Knight

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Athletic footwear and apparel sales worldwide
careerModel.trajectory: Sold Japanese shoes out of car trunk -> partnered with coach Bill Bowerman -> Blue Ribbon Sports -> Nike -> world's largest athletic brand
careerModel.keyDecision: Broke from Japanese supplier Onitsuka to create Nike's own brand, risking everything
careerModel.scaleModel: Outsourced manufacturing combined with elite athlete endorsements and storytelling
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about storytelling: attach your product to people your customers aspire to be

profiles.oneLiner: The cowards never started and the weak died along the way. That leaves us, ladies and gentlemen. Us.

profiles.name: James Dyson

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Premium vacuum cleaners and home appliances
careerModel.trajectory: Art school -> Ballbarrow invention -> 5,127 vacuum prototypes over 5 years -> refused to license -> built multi-billion dollar appliance company
careerModel.keyDecision: Refused to license his technology to established manufacturers, building his own company instead
careerModel.scaleModel: Premium pricing justified by engineering superiority, sold direct to maintain margins
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and care about getting it right: make 5,000 prototypes if needed, then own the whole product rather than licensing

profiles.oneLiner: I made 5,127 prototypes of my vacuum before I got it right. There were 5,126 failures. But I learned from each one.

profiles.name: Edwin Land

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Instant cameras and proprietary film sales
careerModel.trajectory: Harvard dropout -> invented polarizing filter -> Polaroid Corporation -> instant photography -> created demand for products that didn't exist yet
careerModel.keyDecision: Created instant photography from his daughter's question about why she couldn't see a photo right away
careerModel.scaleModel: Razor-and-blade model with cameras as platform and film as recurring revenue
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about wonder: build the product that answers the naive question everyone else ignores

profiles.oneLiner: Don't undertake a project unless it is manifestly important and nearly impossible.

profiles.name: Walt Disney

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Animated films, theme parks, and merchandise licensing
careerModel.trajectory: Failed first animation studio -> created Mickey Mouse -> bet everything on Snow White -> built theme parks -> media empire
careerModel.keyDecision: Bet everything on Snow White as a feature-length animated film when everyone called it 'Disney's Folly'
careerModel.scaleModel: Content IP that compounds across media, parks, merchandise, and experiences
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about magic: treat animation (or any craft) as serious art, then build an ecosystem that multiplies every piece of IP

profiles.oneLiner: We don't make movies to make money, we make money to make more movies.

profiles.name: Henry Ford

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Mass-produced affordable automobiles
careerModel.trajectory: Farm boy -> Edison engineer -> two failed car companies -> Ford Motor -> Model T -> assembly line revolution -> $5/day wage
careerModel.keyDecision: Introduced the moving assembly line, cutting Model T price from $850 to $260 while doubling wages
careerModel.scaleModel: Vertical integration and assembly line efficiency making luxury goods affordable
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and care about access: figure out how to make the expensive thing cheap, and your market becomes everyone

profiles.oneLiner: Don't find fault, find a remedy — anybody can complain.

profiles.name: Andrew Carnegie

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Steel production for railroads and construction
careerModel.trajectory: Penniless Scottish immigrant at 12 -> telegraph operator -> railroad investments -> Carnegie Steel -> sold to JP Morgan -> philanthropy
careerModel.keyDecision: Invested in Bessemer steel technology when competitors stuck with older methods
careerModel.scaleModel: Vertical integration controlling every input from ore to finished steel
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about efficiency: invest in the technology your competitors dismiss, and own every step of the supply chain

profiles.oneLiner: The man who dies rich dies disgraced.

profiles.name: Howard Hughes

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Defense contracts and film production
careerModel.trajectory: Inherited fortune -> record-setting aviator -> film producer -> TWA owner -> increasingly reclusive -> defense contractor
careerModel.keyDecision: Personally set multiple aviation world records to prove his aircraft company's capabilities
careerModel.scaleModel: Personal fame and daring as marketing for industrial ventures
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and care about pushing limits: use personal performance to prove what your company can do

profiles.oneLiner: I want to be remembered for only one thing: my contribution to aviation.

profiles.name: Richard Branson

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Licensing the Virgin brand across diverse businesses
careerModel.trajectory: Student magazine at 16 -> mail-order records -> Virgin Records -> Virgin Atlantic -> 400+ companies across every industry
careerModel.keyDecision: Turned every David-vs-Goliath battle into a media sensation that built the Virgin brand
careerModel.scaleModel: Personal brand as a franchise applied to underserved industries
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about the underdog: build a brand people root for, then apply it to every industry where incumbents are lazy

profiles.oneLiner: Screw it, let's do it.

profiles.name: Michael Dell

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Direct-to-consumer PC sales eliminating middlemen
careerModel.trajectory: Dorm room PC assembly -> Dell Computer -> direct sales revolution -> commoditization -> took company private -> rebuilt
careerModel.keyDecision: Took Dell private to rebuild the company away from Wall Street pressure
careerModel.scaleModel: Direct sales model eliminating retail markup and enabling customization
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about efficiency: cut out the middleman and sell direct, then be willing to go private to rebuild when the model stalls

profiles.oneLiner: Try never to be the smartest person in the room. And if you are, I suggest you invite smarter people or find a different room.

profiles.name: Brad Jacobs

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Operating revenue from consolidated logistics companies
careerModel.trajectory: Started first company at 12 -> serial acquirer across waste, telecom, equipment rental, logistics -> 500+ acquisitions using one repeatable playbook
careerModel.keyDecision: Found and repeated one playbook: buy fragmented industries, roll up, create scale advantages
careerModel.scaleModel: Repeatable roll-up strategy applied to successive fragmented industries
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about scale: find fragmented industries with no dominant player and consolidate them with a repeatable system

profiles.oneLiner: You can mess up a lot of things in business and still do well as long as you get the big trend right.

profiles.name: Sam Walton

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Everyday low prices on consumer goods at massive volume
careerModel.trajectory: Five-and-dime store manager -> opened first Walmart in 1962 -> obsessively drove costs down -> world's largest company
careerModel.keyDecision: Located stores in small towns competitors ignored, building dominance before expanding
careerModel.scaleModel: Cost leadership passed to customers as everyday low prices, funded by supply chain efficiency
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about the customer: obsessively reduce costs and pass every saving along, creating loyalty through value

profiles.oneLiner: There is only one boss — the customer. And he can fire everybody in the company from the chairman on down, simply by spending his money somewhere else.

profiles.name: Coco Chanel

careerModel.primaryRevenue: High fashion and fragrance sales
careerModel.trajectory: Orphanage -> seamstress -> hat maker -> revolutionized women's fashion by stripping away corsets and ornament -> Chanel No. 5 -> global luxury house
careerModel.keyDecision: Made simplicity itself luxurious, liberating women from corsets and excessive ornamentation
careerModel.scaleModel: Personal mythology and cultural revolution turned into an enduring luxury brand
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about freedom: remove what constrains people, and the absence itself becomes the product

profiles.oneLiner: I don't do fashion, I am fashion.

profiles.name: David Ogilvy

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Advertising agency fees and commissions
careerModel.trajectory: Chef -> farmer -> door-to-door stove salesman -> British intelligence -> founded ad agency at 38 with zero experience -> world's most respected agency
careerModel.keyDecision: Founded his agency at 38 with no advertising experience, betting that research-driven creative beats pure intuition
careerModel.scaleModel: Big brand clients attracted by research-proven creative methods and a compelling founder story
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about proof: use research to back your creative instincts, and start your career at any age

profiles.oneLiner: I prefer the discipline of knowledge to the anarchy of ignorance.

profiles.name: Claude Hopkins

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Advertising agency work with performance-based results
careerModel.trajectory: Sweeping church floors as a boy -> copywriter -> invented coupons, split testing, reason-why copy -> wrote Scientific Advertising -> transformed ads from art to science
careerModel.keyDecision: Insisted on measurable results for every ad, inventing split testing and coupon tracking
careerModel.scaleModel: Measurable, repeatable advertising methods that could be taught and scaled
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about proof: make everything measurable, then let the data tell you what works

profiles.oneLiner: The only purpose of advertising is to make sales. It is profitable or unprofitable according to its actual sales.

profiles.name: Arnold Schwarzenegger

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Stacked careers across fitness, real estate, film, and politics
careerModel.trajectory: Austrian village -> Mr. Olympia -> real estate fortune while training -> Hollywood's highest-paid actor -> Governor of California
careerModel.keyDecision: Built a real estate fortune while bodybuilding, so he never needed to accept bad roles
careerModel.scaleModel: Master one domain completely, then transfer the discipline and fame to the next
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about stacking skills: master one domain, use the income to fund the next, and never depend on a single career

profiles.oneLiner: For me life is continuously being hungry. The meaning of life is not simply to exist, to survive, but to move ahead, to go up, to achieve, to conquer.

profiles.name: P.T. Barnum

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Ticket sales for live entertainment spectacles
careerModel.trajectory: Grocery store clerk -> newspaper publisher -> Barnum's American Museum -> circus impresario -> invented modern entertainment marketing
careerModel.keyDecision: Turned every scandal and controversy into free publicity, making his name the brand
careerModel.scaleModel: Controversy as marketing engine, creating spectacles people felt compelled to see
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about attention: turn every controversy into publicity and make your name impossible to ignore

profiles.oneLiner: Every crowd has a silver lining.

profiles.name: Dietrich Mateschitz

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Global energy drink sales at premium prices
careerModel.trajectory: Toothpaste marketing manager -> discovered Thai tonic Krating Daeng -> licensed and repackaged as Red Bull -> created entire energy drink category from nothing
careerModel.keyDecision: Used regulatory bans on Red Bull as free marketing, making the forbidden drink desirable
careerModel.scaleModel: Created a category rather than competing in one, then owned the culture around it through extreme sports
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about creating new markets: don't compete in existing categories, create your own and own the culture around it

profiles.oneLiner: It is a must to believe in one's product. If this was just a marketing gimmick, it would never work.

profiles.name: Todd Graves

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Single-menu chicken finger restaurant chain
careerModel.trajectory: Business plan got worst grade in class -> worked in oil refineries and fishing boats to save money -> opened Raising Cane's -> multi-billion-dollar chain selling only chicken fingers
careerModel.keyDecision: Refused to add menu items despite pressure, keeping only chicken fingers
careerModel.scaleModel: Radical simplicity: one product done perfectly, replicated across thousands of locations
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about focus: do one thing so well that the simplicity itself becomes your competitive advantage

profiles.oneLiner: God made me good at chicken fingers to help people.

profiles.name: Kobe Bryant

careerModel.primaryRevenue: NBA salary, endorsements, then venture capital and media
careerModel.trajectory: High school prodigy -> NBA at 17 -> overcame lack of natural advantages through pure discipline -> 5 championships -> Oscar-winning short film -> venture fund
careerModel.keyDecision: Created the Mamba Mentality framework, turning obsessive practice into a transferable philosophy
careerModel.scaleModel: Personal brand built on work ethic, then transferred to media and venture investing
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about mastery: build a philosophy around your process, then apply that framework to every new domain

profiles.oneLiner: Rest at the end, not in the middle.

profiles.name: Rick Rubin

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Record production fees and label revenue
careerModel.trajectory: NYU dorm room -> co-founded Def Jam Records -> walked away -> started American Recordings -> produced genre-defining albums across hip-hop, rock, country, and metal
careerModel.keyDecision: Left Def Jam at its peak to start fresh with American Recordings, following creative curiosity across genres
careerModel.scaleModel: Reputation for drawing out the essential truth in any artist, transcending genre
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about essence: help people strip away everything that isn't them, and work across genres rather than specializing

profiles.oneLiner: Creativity is not a rare ability. It is not difficult to access. Creativity is a fundamental aspect of being human. It's our birthright.

profiles.name: Sam Zell

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Buying distressed real estate during recessions and holding for recovery
careerModel.trajectory: Bought first building while in college -> specialized in buying distressed properties during recessions -> 'Grave Dancer' -> one of the largest real estate portfolios in America
careerModel.keyDecision: Bought aggressively during recessions when everyone else was selling in panic
careerModel.scaleModel: Contrarian timing: buy when fear is highest and hold through recovery
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about timing: build cash reserves so you can buy what others abandon in downturns

profiles.oneLiner: If everyone is going left, look right.

profiles.name: Ben Franklin

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Printing business and franchise fees from satellite print shops
careerModel.trajectory: Runaway apprentice -> printer -> invented the franchise model -> retired wealthy at 42 -> diplomat, scientist, and founding father
careerModel.keyDecision: Retired from business at 42 to pursue science and public service, funded by passive income from franchised print shops
careerModel.scaleModel: Franchised his print shop model across colonies, earning passive income that funded reinvention
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about freedom: build a business that runs without you, then use the freedom to become who you actually are

profiles.oneLiner: An investment in knowledge pays the best interest.

profiles.name: Thomas Edison

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Patented inventions commercialized through dedicated companies
careerModel.trajectory: Self-educated telegraph operator -> independent inventor -> built world's first industrial research lab at Menlo Park -> GE -> 1,093 patents
careerModel.keyDecision: Built the first industrial research lab, turning invention from solo genius into a scalable team process
careerModel.scaleModel: Industrialized invention itself, with teams testing thousands of materials empirically
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and care about systematic progress: turn your creative process into a team sport with rigorous testing

profiles.oneLiner: I have not failed. I've just found 10,000 ways that won't work.

profiles.name: Levi Strauss

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Durable workwear sold to mass market
careerModel.trajectory: German immigrant dry-goods wholesaler -> partnered with Jacob Davis on riveted jean patent -> created a product so durable it became an American icon
careerModel.keyDecision: Patented the riveted jean with Jacob Davis, escaping commodity wholesaling with a differentiated product
careerModel.scaleModel: One iconic product that became a cultural symbol, replicated at massive scale
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about durability: escape commodity business by making one product so good it becomes a cultural symbol

profiles.oneLiner: The way to do a great deal is to keep on doing a little.

profiles.name: George Lucas

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Merchandising rights and licensing from Star Wars IP
careerModel.trajectory: USC film student -> American Graffiti -> negotiated Star Wars merchandising rights when the studio thought they were worthless -> built Lucasfilm empire
careerModel.keyDecision: Negotiated to keep Star Wars merchandising rights instead of a higher director's fee
careerModel.scaleModel: IP ownership with licensing across every possible consumer product and experience
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about ownership: negotiate to own the intellectual property, not the salary

profiles.oneLiner: Learning to make films is very easy. Learning what to make films about is very hard.

profiles.name: Bernard Arnault

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Portfolio of luxury brands sold at premium margins globally
careerModel.trajectory: Engineering degree -> family construction business -> saw opportunity in luxury -> used a minority stake as Trojan horse to gain control of LVMH -> world's largest luxury group
careerModel.keyDecision: Used a minority stake invitation at Dior as a Trojan horse to seize control of LVMH
careerModel.scaleModel: Acquire heritage luxury brands, install professional management, and let them operate semi-independently
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about excellence: acquire great brands rather than building from scratch, and protect their heritage while professionalizing operations

profiles.oneLiner: Luxury goods are the only area in which it is possible to make luxury margins.

profiles.name: Alexander Graham Bell

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Telephone patent licensing and equipment sales
careerModel.trajectory: Teacher of the deaf -> invented telephone while working on hearing aids -> defended patent against 600+ legal challenges -> AT&T
careerModel.keyDecision: Defended his patent through 600+ legal challenges rather than settling or licensing cheaply
careerModel.scaleModel: Patent monopoly on the most important communication invention of the 19th century
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about connection: solve the problem closest to your heart, and defend your creation fiercely

profiles.oneLiner: When one door closes another door opens; but we so often look so long and so regretfully upon the closed door that we do not see the one which has opened for us.

profiles.name: Walter Chrysler

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Automobile manufacturing and sales
careerModel.trajectory: Railroad mechanic -> locomotive superintendent -> left prestigious railroad career -> joined struggling auto industry -> built Chrysler Corporation into America's third-largest automaker
careerModel.keyDecision: Left a successful railroad career to enter the chaotic early auto industry, seeing where the future was headed
careerModel.scaleModel: Engineering excellence combined with affordable pricing to compete with Ford and GM
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and care about the future: leave the stable industry for the chaotic one when you can see what's coming

profiles.oneLiner: The real secret of success is enthusiasm.

profiles.name: Joseph Pulitzer

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Newspaper advertising and circulation revenue
careerModel.trajectory: Hungarian immigrant -> reporter -> bought failing New York World -> combined investigative journalism with populist spectacle -> most-read newspaper in America
careerModel.keyDecision: Combined serious investigative journalism with populist entertainment, proving quality and popularity aren't opposites
careerModel.scaleModel: Populist spectacle that attracted mass readership, funding serious investigative journalism
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about truth: use entertainment to attract the audience, then use the audience to fund the journalism

profiles.oneLiner: Put it before them briefly so they will read it, clearly so they will understand it, forcibly so they will appreciate it, picturesquely so they will remember it, and above all, accurately so they will be guided by its light.

profiles.name: Andre Agassi

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Tournament winnings and endorsements, then philanthropy and real estate
careerModel.trajectory: Child tennis prodigy forced by his father -> fell from #1 to #141 -> rebuilt game from scratch -> multiple Grand Slams -> built school for at-risk kids in Las Vegas
careerModel.keyDecision: After hitting rock bottom at #141, rebuilt his entire game and identity rather than retiring
careerModel.scaleModel: Personal comeback story as the foundation for a school and charitable platform
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about reinvention: your comeback story becomes the credibility to help others who are stuck

profiles.oneLiner: I play tennis for a living even though I hate tennis, hate it with a dark and secret passion and always have.

profiles.name: Buckminster Fuller

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Lectures, patents, and consulting fees
careerModel.trajectory: Failed businessman -> nearly committed suicide at 32 -> reimagined himself as a human experiment -> geodesic dome -> design science revolution
careerModel.keyDecision: After near-suicide, decided to treat his life as an experiment in what one individual could accomplish
careerModel.scaleModel: Doing more with less (ephemeralization) as a design principle that attracted followers and institutions
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and care about possibility: treat your life as an experiment, and let the results attract the resources

profiles.oneLiner: You never change things by fighting the existing reality. To change something, build a new model that makes the existing model obsolete.

profiles.name: Sam Zemurray

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Banana production, shipping, and distribution
careerModel.trajectory: Penniless immigrant selling ripe bananas off docks -> built banana empire in Honduras -> took over United Fruit Company in a boardroom coup
careerModel.keyDecision: Staged a boardroom coup to take over the much larger United Fruit Company when they underestimated him
careerModel.scaleModel: Hands-on operational knowledge that outcompeted bureaucratic management
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about doing the work yourself: operational knowledge beats boardroom theory every time

profiles.oneLiner: You've been f***ing up this business long enough. I'm going to straighten it out.

profiles.name: Oprah Winfrey

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Television syndication, then diversified media empire
careerModel.trajectory: Childhood abuse and poverty -> local TV news -> The Oprah Winfrey Show -> owned her own production -> OWN network -> billionaire through radical honesty
careerModel.keyDecision: Negotiated ownership of her own show through Harpo Productions rather than accepting a salary
careerModel.scaleModel: Personal authenticity as the brand, scaled through media ownership and book club influence
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about honesty: own the platform, not just the content, and let your vulnerability be your strength

profiles.oneLiner: The biggest adventure you can take is to live the life of your dreams.

profiles.name: Howard Schultz

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Coffee and food sales through company-owned and licensed stores
careerModel.trajectory: Brooklyn projects -> Xerox salesman -> fell in love with Italian espresso bars -> left Starbucks when founders said no -> proved it independently -> bought Starbucks -> 35,000 stores
careerModel.keyDecision: Left Starbucks when they refused his espresso bar vision, proved it independently, then bought Starbucks back
careerModel.scaleModel: Third place experience replicated globally through company-owned stores rather than franchising
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about experience: when the boss says no to your vision, prove it yourself, then come back and buy the company

profiles.oneLiner: I wanted to build the kind of company my father never got a chance to work for.

profiles.name: Nikola Tesla

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Patents and licensing fees for electrical inventions
careerModel.trajectory: Serbian immigrant -> worked for Edison -> quit over broken promises -> invented alternating current -> won War of Currents -> died poor despite powering the modern world
careerModel.keyDecision: Tore up his AC patent royalty contract with Westinghouse to save the company, sacrificing a fortune
careerModel.scaleModel: Superior technology that won on merit despite massive opposition from Edison
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about truth: let the technology speak for itself, but also protect your financial interests

profiles.oneLiner: The present is theirs; the future, for which I really worked, is mine.

profiles.name: Chuck Feeney

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Duty Free Shoppers sales in airports, then strategic giving
careerModel.trajectory: Korean War veteran -> co-founded Duty Free Shoppers -> $8 billion fortune -> secretly gave nearly all of it away -> completed mission to die broke
careerModel.keyDecision: Decided to give away his entire fortune anonymously during his lifetime rather than after death
careerModel.scaleModel: Built wealth through airport retail monopoly, then deployed it as strategic philanthropy
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about impact: giving while living lets you see the results and improve your approach

profiles.oneLiner: I had one idea that never changed in my mind — that you should use your wealth to help people.

profiles.name: Jim Simons

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Performance fees from the most successful hedge fund in history
careerModel.trajectory: NSA codebreaker -> math professor -> applied pattern recognition to financial markets -> Renaissance Technologies -> 66% average annual returns
careerModel.keyDecision: Hired mathematicians and physicists instead of Wall Street traders, building a quant culture
careerModel.scaleModel: Mathematical pattern recognition applied to markets, with extreme secrecy and talent density
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect people and care about patterns: hire from outside your industry and let outsider thinking be your edge

profiles.oneLiner: I did a lot of math. I made a lot of money, and I gave almost all of it away. That's the story of my life.

profiles.name: Sara Blakely

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Direct and retail sales of shapewear products
careerModel.trajectory: Fax machine saleswoman -> invented Spanx with $5,000 and no fashion experience -> bootstrapped to billion-dollar brand -> sold majority stake to Blackstone
careerModel.keyDecision: Bootstrapped entirely without outside investment, maintaining full ownership and creative control
careerModel.scaleModel: One product, one clear problem, word-of-mouth marketing, no outside funding
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about solving a simple problem: bootstrap with your own savings, own 100%, and let the product market itself

profiles.oneLiner: I think failure is nothing more than life's way of nudging you that you are off course.

profiles.name: Melanie Perkins

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Freemium SaaS subscriptions for design tools
careerModel.trajectory: Pitched 100+ investors who all said no -> built Canva with co-founders -> proved concept with real traction -> $40B+ design platform
careerModel.keyDecision: Kept pitching after 100+ rejections, proving the concept with real users rather than slide decks
careerModel.scaleModel: Freemium model making professional design accessible to non-designers at scale
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about access: make the professional tool simple enough for everyone, and prove it with users before investors believe

profiles.oneLiner: I want to empower everyone in the world to design anything and publish anywhere.

profiles.name: Tobi Lütke

careerModel.primaryRevenue: SaaS subscriptions and transaction fees from merchants
careerModel.trajectory: Wanted to sell snowboards online -> couldn't find good software -> built his own -> turned it into Shopify -> powers millions of businesses
careerModel.keyDecision: Bet on the unproven Ruby on Rails framework, prioritizing developer productivity over conventional choices
careerModel.scaleModel: Platform powering millions of merchants, earning from each transaction
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and care about solving your own problem: the tool you build for yourself might be the product millions need

profiles.oneLiner: Amazon is trying to build an empire, and Shopify is trying to arm the rebels.

profiles.name: Ratan Tata

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Diversified industrial group spanning steel, auto, IT, and hospitality
careerModel.trajectory: Born into Tata dynasty -> worked the factory floor -> became chairman -> transformed feudal conglomerate into global powerhouse -> acquired Jaguar Land Rover
careerModel.keyDecision: Forced mandatory retirement ages for subsidiary heads, breaking the feudal power structure
careerModel.scaleModel: Modernization and global acquisition strategy while maintaining founding values of social responsibility
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about modernization: sometimes the hardest leadership is reforming the institution you inherited

profiles.oneLiner: None can destroy iron, but its own rust can. Likewise, none can destroy a person but his own mindset can.

profiles.name: Jack Ma

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Transaction fees and advertising on marketplace platform
careerModel.trajectory: English teacher -> failed the university entrance exam twice -> taught himself English by guiding tourists -> built Alibaba into China's largest e-commerce company with zero technical skills
careerModel.keyDecision: Positioned himself as customer advocate rather than technologist, making Alibaba's mission about enabling small businesses
careerModel.scaleModel: Platform connecting millions of small businesses to buyers, with ecosystem of payment, logistics, and cloud
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about small businesses: you don't need to be technical to build a tech platform if you deeply understand the customer

profiles.oneLiner: Today is hard, tomorrow will be worse, but the day after tomorrow will be sunshine.

profiles.name: Whitney Wolfe Herd

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Freemium subscriptions and in-app purchases
careerModel.trajectory: Co-founded Tinder -> public harassment lawsuit -> turned personal crisis into founding Bumble -> women-make-the-first-move model -> IPO
careerModel.keyDecision: Turned a public harassment crisis into the founding insight for a new product category
careerModel.scaleModel: One clear differentiator (women message first) that created a new dating culture
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about safety: your worst experience might be the founding insight for a product millions need

profiles.oneLiner: The biggest lesson I've learned is that hurt people hurt people, and kindness is just as contagious.

profiles.name: James Sinegal

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Membership fees and thin-margin bulk retail
careerModel.trajectory: Started as Sol Price's protege at FedMart -> co-founded Costco -> refused Wall Street demands to raise margins -> proved low prices and high wages win
careerModel.keyDecision: Refused Wall Street demands to raise margins and cut employee pay, proving the long game wins
careerModel.scaleModel: Membership model with ultra-low margins and high employee wages creating loyalty on both sides
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about doing right: treat employees and customers well even when Wall Street disagrees, and let the results prove it

profiles.oneLiner: When you hire good people, and you provide good jobs and good wages and a career, good things are going to happen.

profiles.name: Alli Webb

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Single-service salon visits and product sales
careerModel.trajectory: Stay-at-home mom doing blowouts for friends -> created Drybar -> blowout-only salon concept nobody thought sustainable -> $100M+ brand
careerModel.keyDecision: Refused to add cuts, color, or other services, keeping only blowouts despite industry pressure
careerModel.scaleModel: Radical single-service focus creating a predictable, replicable customer experience
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about experience: do one thing so well that customers never think to ask for more

profiles.oneLiner: Focus on one thing and be the best at it.

profiles.name: Mackenzie Scott

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Amazon wealth deployed through trust-based giving
careerModel.trajectory: Novelist -> Amazon's first accountant and early driver -> helped build it from garage -> divorce settlement -> pioneered trust-based philanthropy giving billions with no strings attached
careerModel.keyDecision: Gave billions with no strings attached, trusting organizations to know their own needs
careerModel.scaleModel: Rapid, trust-based deployment of capital to organizations already doing the work
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about trust: sometimes the most powerful thing is to give resources without conditions

profiles.oneLiner: I want to de-emphasize privileged voices and cede focus to others.

profiles.name: Tadashi Yanai

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Mass-market basics sold at accessible prices globally
careerModel.trajectory: Single roadside clothing shop in rural Japan -> mastered basics rather than chasing trends -> built Uniqlo into a global fast-fashion empire
careerModel.keyDecision: Focused on perfecting basics (fleece, down, heattech) rather than following fashion trends
careerModel.scaleModel: Technology-driven fabrics at mass-market prices, with minimalist branding
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about basics: master the fundamentals everyone else rushes past, and let quality speak

profiles.oneLiner: I might look successful but I've made many mistakes. People take their failures too seriously. You have to be positive and believe you will find success next time.

profiles.name: Masayoshi Son

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Returns from massive technology bets through SoftBank Vision Fund
careerModel.trajectory: Korean-Japanese student -> UC Berkeley -> started SoftBank -> early bet on Yahoo Japan and Alibaba -> Vision Fund -> world's most influential tech investor
careerModel.keyDecision: Invested $20M in Alibaba in 2000 based on a 5-minute meeting with Jack Ma, which became worth over $100B
careerModel.scaleModel: Massive conviction-driven bets on companies that could dominate entire categories
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about vision: make a few massive bets based on conviction rather than many safe ones based on consensus

profiles.oneLiner: Think big; think disruptive. Execute with full passion.

profiles.name: Arianna Huffington

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Advertising revenue (HuffPost), then corporate wellness services (Thrive)
careerModel.trajectory: Greek immigrant -> political commentator -> built Huffington Post from blog to most-read news site -> sold to AOL for $315M -> pivoted to wellness with Thrive Global
careerModel.keyDecision: Pivoted from media to wellness after collapsing from exhaustion, turning personal crisis into a business
careerModel.scaleModel: Personal brand and thought leadership monetized through media, then corporate consulting
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about sustainability: your burnout story might be the most valuable thing you have to share

profiles.oneLiner: Burnout is not the price we have to pay for success.

profiles.name: Hamdi Ulukaya

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Yogurt sales through grocery retail channels
careerModel.trajectory: Turkish immigrant -> spotted shuttered Kraft yogurt factory -> bought it for $700K -> spent 2 years perfecting Greek yogurt -> built Chobani into multi-billion-dollar brand
careerModel.keyDecision: Bought a shuttered factory that a major corporation had abandoned, seeing value where others saw failure
careerModel.scaleModel: Superior product in an underserved category, scaled through existing retail distribution
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and care about quality: buy what big companies abandon and make it better than they ever could

profiles.oneLiner: The minute a refugee gets a job is the minute they stop being a refugee.

profiles.name: Tory Burch

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Accessible luxury fashion sold direct and through department stores
careerModel.trajectory: Fashion PR and marketing roles -> spotted white space between luxury and accessible -> launched brand -> sold $7.5M on first day of website -> global accessible luxury brand
careerModel.keyDecision: Targeted the gap between true luxury and mass market that no major brand occupied
careerModel.scaleModel: Accessible luxury positioning with strong e-commerce and social media from day one
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about taste: find the price point gap that nobody is serving and position yourself precisely there

profiles.oneLiner: When I started my company, I saw a void in the market for chic, beautifully made pieces that didn't cost a fortune.

profiles.name: Bobbi Brown

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Natural-look cosmetics sold through prestige retail
careerModel.trajectory: Started with 10 lipsticks and a philosophy that women should look like themselves -> built into powerhouse -> sold to Estee Lauder for $74.5M -> later launched new media and wellness brand
careerModel.keyDecision: Built an entire brand on the philosophy that makeup should make women look like themselves, not someone else
careerModel.scaleModel: Authentic philosophy that attracted loyal customers, then scaled through prestige retail acquisition
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about authenticity: build a brand around helping people be more themselves, not someone else

profiles.oneLiner: I believe that all women are pretty without makeup — but with the right makeup can be pretty powerful.

profiles.name: Jose Andres

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Restaurant group revenue and philanthropic donations for World Central Kitchen
careerModel.trajectory: Spanish chef -> 30+ restaurant empire in US -> founded World Central Kitchen -> served 350+ million meals in disasters worldwide
careerModel.keyDecision: Founded World Central Kitchen, turning restaurant logistics expertise into the world's fastest disaster relief organization
careerModel.scaleModel: Restaurant supply chain expertise repurposed for disaster relief at unprecedented speed
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about feeding people: the operational skills from one domain might solve a completely different problem at global scale

profiles.oneLiner: The business of feeding people is the most amazing business in the world.

profiles.name: Patagonia's Rose Marcario

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Premium outdoor apparel sales under mission-driven brand
careerModel.trajectory: Finance and private equity career -> joined Patagonia as CFO -> CEO -> took revenue from $600M to $1B while suing the US government over public lands
careerModel.keyDecision: Sued the US government over public lands reduction while simultaneously growing the business, proving activism and profit aren't opposites
careerModel.scaleModel: Financial rigor applied to a mission-driven company, proving environmental activism supercharges revenue
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about the environment: financial discipline makes activism more credible, not less

profiles.oneLiner: Profit is important, but profit isn't the only measure of success.

profiles.name: Stewart Butterfield

careerModel.primaryRevenue: SaaS subscriptions for team communication
careerModel.trajectory: Failed at building a video game twice -> both pivots became massive: Flickr (sold to Yahoo) and Slack (sold to Salesforce for $27.7B)
careerModel.keyDecision: Recognized that the internal tool his team built was more valuable than the game they were making
careerModel.scaleModel: Internal tool discovered during failed project, then scaled as standalone SaaS product
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about how teams work: pay attention to the tools you build for yourself along the way, they might be the real product

profiles.oneLiner: We don't sell saddles here. What we are selling is organizational transformation.

profiles.name: Jesse Itzler

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Built and sold multiple businesses across unrelated industries
careerModel.trajectory: Aspiring rapper -> jingle writer -> founded Marquis Jet through cold-calling -> Zico coconut water -> ultramarathon running -> serial entrepreneur and speaker
careerModel.keyDecision: Built Marquis Jet to $1B in revenue with zero aviation experience purely through relentless cold-calling
careerModel.scaleModel: Personal energy and sales ability applied to whatever industry seemed interesting
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about variety: sales skills transfer to any industry, so follow your curiosity and sell your way in

profiles.oneLiner: Built a life around collecting experiences, not credentials. Life resumes over paper ones.

profiles.name: Daymond John

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Fashion brand sales, then media and venture investing
careerModel.trajectory: Sewing hats in mother's Queens house -> got LL Cool J to wear FUBU for free -> $350M fashion brand -> Shark Tank investor -> branding empire
careerModel.keyDecision: Got LL Cool J to wear FUBU in a Gap commercial for free, proving grassroots marketing beats advertising
careerModel.scaleModel: Cultural credibility through organic celebrity adoption, not paid endorsement
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about culture: get one tastemaker to authentically use your product rather than paying for advertising

profiles.oneLiner: It doesn't matter how many times you fail. It doesn't matter how many times you almost get it right. No one is going to know or care about your failures, and neither should you.

profiles.name: Sophia Amoruso

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Vintage clothing sales through eBay, then branded e-commerce
careerModel.trajectory: Dumpster diver -> eBay vintage clothing hustle -> Nasty Gal grew to $100M+ in 5 years through social media storytelling -> bankruptcy -> Girlboss media brand
careerModel.keyDecision: Mastered social media storytelling before anyone else in fashion, making the brand voice the product
careerModel.scaleModel: Social media storytelling creating a community around a curated brand identity
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about curation: your taste and voice can be the brand, but you also need operational skills to scale it

profiles.oneLiner: A #GIRLBOSS is someone who's in charge of her own life. She gets what she wants because she works for it.

profiles.name: Vera Wang

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Bridal gowns and occasion wear at luxury price points
careerModel.trajectory: Failed Olympic figure skater -> Vogue editor for 17 years -> passed over for editor-in-chief -> started bridal line at 40 -> redefined the wedding industry
careerModel.keyDecision: Started a new career in bridal fashion at 40 after two major rejections (Olympics, Vogue)
careerModel.scaleModel: Celebrity bridal clients created aspirational demand that cascaded to broader market through licensing
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about beauty: two rejections might just be redirecting you to the field you were meant to own

profiles.oneLiner: When I decided to get married at 40, I couldn't find a dress with the modernity or sophistication I wanted. That's when I saw the opportunity for a wedding gown business.

profiles.name: Tony Hsieh

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Online shoe and apparel sales with exceptional customer service
careerModel.trajectory: Sold LinkExchange to Microsoft for $265M -> bet everything on Zappos -> proved online shoe sales work with free shipping both ways -> sold to Amazon for $1.2B
careerModel.keyDecision: Offered free shipping both ways when everyone said online shoe sales were impossible
careerModel.scaleModel: Customer happiness as the product, with shoes as the delivery mechanism
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about customer experience: remove every risk the customer faces, and they'll become your marketing team

profiles.oneLiner: Chase the vision, not the money — the money will end up following you.

profiles.name: Indra Nooyi

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Global snack and beverage sales (PepsiCo)
careerModel.trajectory: Indian immigrant -> BCG consultant -> Motorola -> PepsiCo strategist -> CEO -> transformed PepsiCo with 'Performance with Purpose' toward healthier products
careerModel.keyDecision: Pivoted PepsiCo toward healthier products with 'Performance with Purpose' when critics mocked the strategy
careerModel.scaleModel: Mission-driven transformation of a legacy company, proving health and profit align long-term
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about health: transform the existing institution from within rather than starting from scratch

profiles.oneLiner: Whatever anybody says or does, assume positive intent. You will be amazed at how your whole approach to a person or problem becomes very different.

profiles.name: Fred Rogers

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Public broadcasting funding and licensing
careerModel.trajectory: Presbyterian seminary -> children's television pioneer -> Mister Rogers' Neighborhood for 33 years -> cultural icon
careerModel.keyDecision: Refused merchandising and scaling, insisting every interaction be slow, real, and one-to-one
careerModel.scaleModel: One unchanging show broadcast nationally for decades, reaching generations through repetition and trust
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about children: choose depth over scale, and let decades of consistency be your growth strategy

profiles.oneLiner: Treated every child as a person worthy of a slow, unhurried reply.

profiles.name: Maria Montessori

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Teacher training programs and method licensing worldwide
careerModel.trajectory: First female doctor in Italy -> worked with 'uneducable' children -> proved her method in Casa dei Bambini -> trained teachers globally -> method adopted worldwide
careerModel.keyDecision: Applied her method to typically developing children after proving it worked with institutionalized children
careerModel.scaleModel: Trained teachers who opened their own schools, spreading the method organically worldwide
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about education: create a replicable method, train others to teach it, and let them carry it further than you could alone

profiles.oneLiner: Watched children so carefully that the furniture, the tools, and the timetable all eventually bent to what she saw.

profiles.name: Anne Sullivan

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Employment as Helen Keller's teacher and companion for 49 years
careerModel.trajectory: Near-blind orphan at Perkins School for the Blind -> arrived in Tuscumbia at 20 -> taught Helen Keller -> 49 years as companion and instructor
careerModel.keyDecision: Abandoned formal curriculum in favor of spelling words into Helen's palm whenever she reached for something
careerModel.scaleModel: One student, 49 years of devotion, proving that the deepest teaching defies efficiency
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about unlocking potential: sometimes your life's work is one person, and that is enough

profiles.oneLiner: Spelled the world into another person's hand, one word at a time, for almost half a century.

profiles.name: Janusz Korczak

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Orphanage direction, medical practice, and writing
careerModel.trajectory: Pediatrician -> opened Dom Sierot orphanage in 1912 -> wrote extensively on children's rights -> radio broadcaster -> walked with 192 orphans to Treblinka
careerModel.keyDecision: Refused offers to escape the Warsaw Ghetto, staying with his 192 orphans
careerModel.scaleModel: One orphanage run as a model of children's self-governance, with writing that influenced global child rights
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about children's dignity: build one institution that proves your principles, and write about it so the idea outlasts you

profiles.oneLiner: Built a republic of children and then refused to let them walk into the dark alone.

profiles.name: Vivian Gussin Paley

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University lab school teaching salary and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Kindergarten teacher at University of Chicago Lab Schools -> audio-recorded her classroom for decades -> published influential books on how children think and play
careerModel.keyDecision: Started tape-recording her own classroom, turning daily teaching into publishable research
careerModel.scaleModel: Decades of classroom observation published as narrative research that influenced teaching worldwide
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about listening: record and study your own practice, and the insights will become books that change your field

profiles.oneLiner: Turned a five-year-old's dictated story into a research method and a moral instrument.

profiles.name: T. Berry Brazelton

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Harvard medical position, books, and television
careerModel.trajectory: Harvard pediatrician -> created Neonatal Behavioral Assessment Scale -> 24+ books -> television show -> changed how doctors see babies
careerModel.keyDecision: Treated babies as individuals with observable preferences from birth, when the field saw them as blank slates
careerModel.scaleModel: Clinical assessment tool (NBAS) adopted worldwide, with books and TV translating the science for parents
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about seeing individuals: create a tool that makes your insight systematic, then write and broadcast to spread it

profiles.oneLiner: Insisted that a newborn already had a point of view, and built a 28-item scale to prove it.

profiles.name: Emmi Pikler

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Orphanage direction and pediatric practice
careerModel.trajectory: Hungarian pediatrician -> founded Loczy orphanage in 1946 -> developed infant care approach centered on uninterrupted free movement -> directed it for 33 years
careerModel.keyDecision: Proved that orphanage children could develop normally without constant adult intervention, through respectful care
careerModel.scaleModel: One model institution whose methods were documented and adopted by childcare centers worldwide
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about respect: build one institution that proves your philosophy, and document everything so others can replicate it

profiles.oneLiner: Made bathing and nappy-changing into the main classroom.

profiles.name: Mary Ainsworth

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University salary and research grants
careerModel.trajectory: Developmental psychologist -> fieldwork in Uganda -> created the Strange Situation procedure -> built empirical foundation for attachment theory
careerModel.keyDecision: Created the Strange Situation procedure, giving attachment theory a measurable, replicable test
careerModel.scaleModel: One experimental procedure that became the standard assessment tool for an entire field of psychology
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about proof: invent one procedure that makes your theory testable, and it will outlive every book you write

profiles.oneLiner: Invented an eight-part lab test for something as slippery as a baby's trust.

profiles.name: Paul Farmer

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Grants and donations for Partners In Health
careerModel.trajectory: Harvard medical anthropologist -> co-founded Partners In Health in 1987 -> proved the rural poor deserve the same treatment as Harvard patients -> changed global health policy
careerModel.keyDecision: Refused to accept lower treatment standards for poor patients, proving world-class care was possible anywhere
careerModel.scaleModel: Prove it works in one community, then use the evidence to change global health policy
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about equity: prove your highest standard works in the hardest setting, then use the proof to change the system

profiles.oneLiner: Treated walking eight hours to reach one patient as a clinical standard, not a sacrifice.

profiles.name: Virginia Apgar

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Medical practice and March of Dimes leadership
careerModel.trajectory: Surgeon redirected to anesthesiology -> created the Apgar score for newborns in 1953 -> became VP at March of Dimes -> public voice for birth defects prevention
careerModel.keyDecision: Created a simple 1-minute scoring system for newborn health that any doctor or nurse could use
careerModel.scaleModel: One simple scoring tool adopted universally, saving millions of lives through early intervention
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about saving lives: create one simple tool that anyone can use, and its simplicity will be its power

profiles.oneLiner: Answered a resident's casual question by scribbling on a napkin, and the scribble became the standard check every newborn on Earth now gets.

profiles.name: Cicely Saunders

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Hospital operation and charitable donations
careerModel.trajectory: Nurse -> social worker -> trained as doctor to gain authority -> founded St Christopher's Hospice in 1967 -> created the modern hospice movement
careerModel.keyDecision: Trained as a doctor specifically to gain the authority needed to revolutionize end-of-life care
careerModel.scaleModel: One model hospice that proved the concept, then inspired thousands of hospices worldwide
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about dignity: get the credentials you need to be taken seriously, then build one institution that proves everything

profiles.oneLiner: Kept re-qualifying until nobody in the hospital could tell her she wasn't allowed to sit with the dying.

profiles.name: Irena Sendler

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Social work salary
careerModel.trajectory: Polish social worker -> helped smuggle Jewish children out of Warsaw Ghetto during WWII -> arrested and tortured -> survived -> recognized decades later
careerModel.keyDecision: Used her social worker credentials to enter the Ghetto legally, then built a network to smuggle children out
careerModel.scaleModel: Professional access combined with underground networks to save approximately 2,500 children
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about justice: use whatever legitimate access you have as a doorway for the work that matters

profiles.oneLiner: Kept the list of rescued children in jars under an apple tree so the identities could survive the war even if she didn't.

profiles.name: Wangari Maathai

careerModel.primaryRevenue: International grants and awards for Green Belt Movement
careerModel.trajectory: First East African woman PhD -> founded Green Belt Movement in 1977 -> planted 30 million trees -> first African woman Nobel Peace Prize winner
careerModel.keyDecision: Connected tree planting to women's empowerment, making environmentalism a democracy movement
careerModel.scaleModel: Community-based tree planting that simultaneously addressed deforestation, poverty, and women's agency
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about the environment: tie your environmental work to the economic empowerment of the people doing it

profiles.oneLiner: Paid rural women a few shillings per seedling and grew a democracy movement sideways out of a tree nursery.

profiles.name: John Wooden

careerModel.primaryRevenue: UCLA coaching salary, then books and speaking
careerModel.trajectory: English teacher -> basketball coach -> 10 NCAA championships in 12 years -> 88-game winning streak -> most successful coach in college basketball history
careerModel.keyDecision: Built his coaching philosophy around character and preparation rather than winning, which produced the most winning record ever
careerModel.scaleModel: A teaching philosophy (Pyramid of Success) that produced results and became a self-reinforcing brand
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about character: focus on preparation and process, and the wins take care of themselves

profiles.oneLiner: Coached the best athletes in college basketball by starting each season teaching them how to put on their socks.

profiles.name: Carl Sagan

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Cornell professorship, books, and television
careerModel.trajectory: Planetary scientist at Cornell -> co-wrote and narrated Cosmos -> bestselling author -> made astronomy feel personal for millions
careerModel.keyDecision: Chose to communicate science to the public through television, risking academic credibility
careerModel.scaleModel: Television series that reached hundreds of millions, combined with bestselling books
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about wonder: use the medium with the widest reach, even if your peers disapprove

profiles.oneLiner: Took the scale of the universe and kept finding metaphors small enough to fit in a human chest.

profiles.name: David Attenborough

careerModel.primaryRevenue: BBC broadcasting contracts and production fees
careerModel.trajectory: Joined BBC in 1952 -> controller of BBC2 -> chose fieldwork over management -> 70+ years of natural history broadcasting -> most traveled person in television history
careerModel.keyDecision: Turned down the BBC Director General position to return to making programs, choosing craft over power
careerModel.scaleModel: Partnership with one institution (BBC) for 70+ years, building a body of work no competitor can match
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about the natural world: choose the work over the title, and let longevity be your competitive advantage

profiles.oneLiner: Got out of the frame so the animals could take it.

profiles.name: Jacob Bronowski

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Academic positions and BBC television production
careerModel.trajectory: Polish-British mathematician -> government science advisor -> created The Ascent of Man for BBC -> delivered one of the most powerful moments in television history at Auschwitz
careerModel.keyDecision: Created a 13-part history of human knowledge for television, treating science as a humanistic story
careerModel.scaleModel: One landmark television series that redefined how science could be presented to the public
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about knowledge: frame science as a human story, not a set of facts, and people will listen

profiles.oneLiner: Walked into the ash pond at Auschwitz so the camera could hear him refuse absolute certainty.

profiles.name: Oliver Sacks

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Medical practice, university salary, and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Neurologist at Beth Abraham Hospital -> turned individual patients into narrative essays -> bestselling author -> one of the most beloved science writers of the 20th century
careerModel.keyDecision: Published Awakenings and The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat, turning clinical neurology into literature
careerModel.scaleModel: Clinical case studies written as narrative literature that reached millions of general readers
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about patients: write about the people you serve with the depth they deserve, and the world will read it

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote about his patients the way a novelist writes about characters, because he thought the clinic was cheating them otherwise.

profiles.name: Julia Child

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Television production, books, and cooking classes
careerModel.trajectory: OSS intelligence officer in WWII -> moved to Paris at 36 -> co-wrote Mastering the Art of French Cooking -> launched The French Chef on WGBH -> made French cooking accessible to Americans
careerModel.keyDecision: Started a career in cooking at 36 with no professional training, proving passion beats credentials
careerModel.scaleModel: Television personality making the intimidating feel accessible through warmth and humor
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about demystifying: start your real career at any age, and use humor to make the intimidating feel approachable

profiles.oneLiner: Kept the mistakes in on live television so the viewer at home would believe they could do it too.

profiles.name: Isaiah Berlin

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Oxford professorship and publications
careerModel.trajectory: Russian-born -> Oxford philosopher -> BBC Reith Lectures -> founding president of Wolfson College -> leading voice on liberty and value pluralism
careerModel.keyDecision: Shifted from analytical philosophy to the history of ideas, following his real intellectual passion
careerModel.scaleModel: BBC lectures and essays that made complex philosophical ideas accessible to educated general audiences
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about ideas: follow your intellectual curiosity even when it takes you away from your field's mainstream

profiles.oneLiner: Talked his essays out in one long stream at 200 words a minute and let the secretary catch them.

profiles.name: Lynn Margulis

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University salary and research grants
careerModel.trajectory: Biologist -> 1967 paper on serial endosymbiosis rejected by 15 journals -> eventually became foundational in modern cell biology -> Distinguished University Professor at UMass
careerModel.keyDecision: Persisted through 15 journal rejections to publish her endosymbiosis theory, which became foundational
careerModel.scaleModel: One paradigm-shifting paper that rewrote cell biology, vindicated over decades
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about truth: persist through rejection when the evidence is on your side, because paradigm shifts take decades

profiles.oneLiner: Got her paper rejected about fifteen times and won.

profiles.name: E.O. Wilson

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Harvard professorship, books, and Pulitzer Prizes
careerModel.trajectory: Ant specialist -> Sociobiology (1975) caused a firestorm -> two Pulitzer Prizes -> biodiversity advocate -> Half-Earth proposal
careerModel.keyDecision: Published Sociobiology despite knowing it would provoke furious backlash, because the science demanded it
careerModel.scaleModel: Controversial academic work that attracted attention, then popular books that built a conservation movement
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about nature: publish the truth even when it's controversial, then use the attention to build a conservation movement

profiles.oneLiner: Stared at ants under rotting bark at age nine and never really looked away.

profiles.name: Joseph Campbell

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Sarah Lawrence teaching salary, books, and later PBS series
careerModel.trajectory: Lived in a shack during the Depression reading for 5 years -> professor at Sarah Lawrence for 38 years -> The Hero with a Thousand Faces -> PBS Power of Myth series with Bill Moyers made him famous at 83
careerModel.keyDecision: Spent 5 years in self-directed reading during the Depression, building the knowledge base for his life's work
careerModel.scaleModel: Decades of teaching crystallized into books, then a PBS series at 83 that reached millions
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about meaning: invest years in deep reading before you try to teach, and fame may come late but it will come

profiles.oneLiner: Found the same story hiding in every culture and taught it for 38 years.

profiles.name: Susan Sontag

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties, magazine essays, and university positions
careerModel.trajectory: Precocious reader -> Berkeley at 15 -> married at 17, divorced at 26 -> moved to NYC -> Notes on Camp made her famous -> leading American intellectual for 40 years
careerModel.keyDecision: Published Notes on Camp in 1964, claiming popular culture as worthy of serious intellectual attention
careerModel.scaleModel: Magazine essays that set the terms of cultural debate, backed by prestige books
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about culture: write the essay that reframes how people see something they already know

profiles.oneLiner: Directed Waiting for Godot by candlelight in a city under siege.

profiles.name: Claude Lévi-Strauss

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Academic positions and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: French philosopher -> fieldwork in Brazil -> founded structural anthropology -> published Tristes Tropiques -> chair at College de France
careerModel.keyDecision: Applied structural linguistics to anthropology, creating an entirely new analytical framework
careerModel.scaleModel: One theoretical framework that reorganized how anthropology was done worldwide
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about pattern: borrow a method from another field and apply it to yours, and you might create a new discipline

profiles.oneLiner: Treated a Nambikwara village and a Parisian kinship chart as the same kind of sentence.

profiles.name: Svante Pääbo

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Max Planck Institute directorship and Nobel Prize
careerModel.trajectory: Swedish geneticist -> attempted to extract DNA from mummies as a student -> founded the field of paleogenetics -> sequenced Neanderthal genome -> Nobel Prize 2022
careerModel.keyDecision: Pursued ancient DNA extraction when everyone said it was impossible, creating an entirely new field
careerModel.scaleModel: Created a new scientific field (paleogenetics) by developing techniques no one thought were possible
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about the past: pursue the impossible technique, because founding a new field is the ultimate career security

profiles.oneLiner: Learned to sequence DNA out of bones older than farming, and found whole branches of humanity nobody had known were there.

profiles.name: Jane Jacobs

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and journalism
careerModel.trajectory: Journalist with no formal training in urban planning -> wrote The Death and Life of Great American Cities -> defeated Robert Moses's expressway -> changed how cities think about themselves
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote The Death and Life of Great American Cities as a journalist, challenging the entire urban planning profession from outside
careerModel.scaleModel: One book that changed a profession, written by an outsider who observed what the experts missed
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about cities: you don't need credentials to see what experts miss, just observation and courage

profiles.oneLiner: Took her eyes on her own Greenwich Village block and turned them into an argument that beat Robert Moses.

profiles.name: Ella Baker

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Organizing salary from NAACP and SCLC
careerModel.trajectory: NAACP field organizer -> helped found SCLC -> convened the meeting that created SNCC -> trained a generation of civil rights leaders -> chose to stay behind the scenes
careerModel.keyDecision: Chose grassroots leadership development over personal fame, training others to lead rather than leading herself
