careerModel.scaleModel: Train leaders who train leaders, creating a self-replicating movement
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about justice: train other leaders rather than building your own platform, and your impact will multiply

profiles.oneLiner: Believed that the moment a movement depended on a single man was the moment it had already lost.

profiles.name: Dorothy Height

careerModel.primaryRevenue: National Council of Negro Women leadership
careerModel.trajectory: Social worker -> led National Council of Negro Women for 32 years -> key organizer of 1963 March on Washington -> one of the least credited civil rights leaders
careerModel.keyDecision: Led from behind the scenes for decades, building infrastructure rather than seeking credit
careerModel.scaleModel: Institutional leadership that outlasted any single campaign, building infrastructure for decades of work
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about equality: build the institution, not just the campaign, and let the work speak

profiles.oneLiner: Ran an entire civil rights organisation for 32 years while her male peers took the microphones.

profiles.name: Bayard Rustin

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Organizing work and institutional leadership
careerModel.trajectory: Pacifist -> trained MLK in Gandhian nonviolence -> organized the 1963 March on Washington -> sidelined because he was openly gay -> vindicated decades later
careerModel.keyDecision: Organized the March on Washington while knowing his sexuality would be used to attack the movement
careerModel.scaleModel: Operational genius behind the scenes, organizing the logistics that made historic moments possible
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about justice: do the essential work even when you can't take credit for it

profiles.oneLiner: Put 250,000 people on the National Mall in eight weeks and then had to leave the stage before anyone saw him.

profiles.name: Fannie Lou Hamer

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Movement organizing and cooperative farming
careerModel.trajectory: Mississippi sharecropper -> tried to register to vote at 44 -> beaten and fired -> became one of the most powerful orators of the voting rights movement -> founded Freedom Farm Cooperative
careerModel.keyDecision: Founded the Freedom Farm Cooperative, connecting voting rights to economic independence
careerModel.scaleModel: Personal testimony so powerful it changed national politics, combined with practical economic alternatives
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about freedom: tell your own story so powerfully that it becomes impossible to ignore, then build something practical

profiles.oneLiner: Sang hymns in a Winona jail cell with her kidneys failing and came out louder than the governor of Mississippi.

profiles.name: Grace Lee Boggs

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Organizing, writing, and speaking
careerModel.trajectory: Chinese-American philosopher -> moved to Detroit -> 62 years of community organizing -> co-author of Revolution and Evolution -> living through every major social movement of the 20th century
careerModel.keyDecision: Committed to one city (Detroit) for 62 years rather than chasing movements across the country
careerModel.scaleModel: Rootedness in one place for decades, allowing deep community transformation
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about community: stay in one place long enough to see real change, because depth beats breadth

profiles.oneLiner: Kept starting over every decade for 70 years and never ran out of Detroit.

profiles.name: Saul Alinsky

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Foundation support for organizing work and consulting
careerModel.trajectory: Chicago sociologist -> founded Industrial Areas Foundation in 1940 -> wrote Rules for Radicals -> built the template for modern community organizing
careerModel.keyDecision: Codified community organizing into a teachable, repeatable method in Rules for Radicals
careerModel.scaleModel: Created a replicable organizing methodology trained through institutions that outlived him
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about power: codify your method so others can use it without you

profiles.oneLiner: Taught that power belongs to the people who are willing to be a visible nuisance first.

profiles.name: Václav Havel

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Playwriting, then presidential salary
careerModel.trajectory: Playwright -> dissident -> co-founded Charter 77 -> wrote The Power of the Powerless -> imprisoned -> became first post-Communist president of Czechoslovakia
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote The Power of the Powerless, arguing that 'living in truth' was itself a political act against totalitarianism
careerModel.scaleModel: Artistic integrity as political resistance, building moral authority that became political power
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about truth: living honestly is a political act, and moral authority can become real power when the moment comes

profiles.oneLiner: Treated a rock band trial as a constitutional crisis and lived to see the frame win.

profiles.name: Harriet Tubman

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Intermittent work and supporter donations
careerModel.trajectory: Escaped slavery in 1849 -> returned to the South 13 times -> guided ~70 people to freedom -> Union spy and scout -> never lost a passenger
careerModel.keyDecision: Returned to the South repeatedly after escaping, risking recapture each time
careerModel.scaleModel: Personal courage combined with meticulous operational planning, creating a network others could use
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about freedom: go back for the people still trapped, and build a system that works even in danger

profiles.oneLiner: Went back into the dark thirteen times after she had already gotten out.

profiles.name: Frederick Douglass

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Speaking fees, newspaper publishing, and book sales
careerModel.trajectory: Escaped slavery in 1838 -> self-taught orator -> published Narrative of the Life -> founded The North Star newspaper -> most influential Black voice in 19th-century America
careerModel.keyDecision: Published his autobiography despite the risk of recapture, because the truth was more important than safety
careerModel.scaleModel: Personal testimony amplified through speaking tours, newspaper, and books across decades
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about freedom: tell your own story publicly even when it's dangerous, because authentic testimony is the most powerful tool

profiles.oneLiner: Taught himself to read and then spent a lifetime making white America listen to what he had read.

profiles.name: Jane Addams

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Donations, government funding, and personal wealth
careerModel.trajectory: Wealthy woman searching for purpose -> co-founded Hull House in 1889 -> created the model for social work -> first American woman Nobel Peace Prize
careerModel.keyDecision: Moved into an immigrant neighborhood and lived there, rather than serving from a distance
careerModel.scaleModel: One settlement house that became the model for social services nationwide
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about community: move in rather than commute in, and let proximity be your method

profiles.oneLiner: Moved into the slum on purpose and kept the door unlocked for 46 years.

profiles.name: Dorothy Day

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Catholic Worker newspaper sales (1 cent per copy) and donations
careerModel.trajectory: Journalist and bohemian -> conversion to Catholicism -> co-founded Catholic Worker movement in 1933 -> combined radical pacifism with direct hospitality for 47 years
careerModel.keyDecision: Combined radical political activism with direct daily service to the homeless, refusing to separate theory from practice
careerModel.scaleModel: Catholic Worker houses replicated independently across cities, each self-governing
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about the poor: serve people directly every day while also challenging the system, and let others replicate the model freely

profiles.oneLiner: Sold a newspaper for a penny on Union Square and turned it into houses that fed strangers for the rest of the century.

profiles.name: Studs Terkel

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Radio show and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Chicago radio host for 45 years -> oral history books (Working, The Good War) -> Pulitzer Prize -> the great listener of American life
careerModel.keyDecision: Chose oral history as his form, letting other people's voices carry the story instead of his own
careerModel.scaleModel: Radio show as daily practice that fed book-length oral histories, each capturing an era
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about stories: make listening your craft, and the books will write themselves from what people tell you

profiles.oneLiner: Turned the country's anonymous cab drivers, waitresses and steelworkers into the authors of its history.

profiles.name: Jimmy Carter

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Carter Center funded by donations, plus books and speaking
careerModel.trajectory: Navy -> peanut farmer -> Governor -> 39th President -> lost reelection -> founded Carter Center -> 40+ years of disease eradication and peace work -> Habitat for Humanity
careerModel.keyDecision: Built a post-presidency more impactful than most presidencies through the Carter Center
careerModel.scaleModel: Institutional platform (Carter Center) for election monitoring, disease eradication, and peacebuilding
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about service: your second act can be bigger than your first if you build an institution around it

profiles.oneLiner: Lost an election and then spent 44 years proving that the post-presidency was the real job.

profiles.name: Desmond Tutu

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Church positions and Nobel Prize platform
careerModel.trajectory: Teacher -> Anglican priest -> Bishop of Johannesburg -> first Black Archbishop of Cape Town -> chaired Truth and Reconciliation Commission -> Nobel Peace Prize 1984
careerModel.keyDecision: Chaired the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, choosing restorative justice over retribution
careerModel.scaleModel: Moral authority from religious leadership applied to political transformation
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about healing: sometimes the most radical act is choosing forgiveness over punishment as a national strategy

profiles.oneLiner: Turned confession and listening into state-level infrastructure for a country that had no playbook for peace.

profiles.name: Nawal El Saadawi

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Books and psychiatry practice
careerModel.trajectory: Egyptian physician -> dismissed from government for writing about women's issues -> imprisoned -> founded Arab Women's Solidarity Association -> 50+ books on the condition of Arab women
careerModel.keyDecision: Continued writing and speaking about women's rights despite imprisonment and death threats
careerModel.scaleModel: Prolific publishing (50+ books) that built an unavoidable body of evidence across decades
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about women's freedom: keep writing even when they imprison you, because volume makes the message impossible to suppress

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote her way out of a prison cell with eyebrow pencil on toilet paper, and kept writing until she had built a movement.

profiles.name: Toni Morrison

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties, Princeton professorship, and Nobel Prize
careerModel.trajectory: First Black woman senior fiction editor at Random House -> published other Black writers -> wrote her own novels -> Nobel Prize 1993 -> Princeton professor
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote the books she wanted to read, filling the gap in American literature she saw as an editor
careerModel.scaleModel: Literary fiction that became essential American reading, sustained by teaching and prizes
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about representation: write what's missing from the culture, and edit others who are doing the same

profiles.oneLiner: Edited the books that built the Black canon with one hand and wrote the ones that finished it with the other.

profiles.name: James Baldwin

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and magazine essays
careerModel.trajectory: Harlem preacher's son -> left for Paris with $40 -> wrote Go Tell It on the Mountain, Notes of a Native Son -> became the moral voice of the civil rights era
careerModel.keyDecision: Left America for Paris to find the distance needed to write about race in America
careerModel.scaleModel: Exile as creative strategy, writing essays that reshaped the American conversation
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about truth: sometimes you need to leave to see clearly, and the distance makes the writing sharper

profiles.oneLiner: Translated private humiliation into public argument with the precision of a courtroom stenographer.

profiles.name: Seamus Heaney

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Poetry collections, university positions, and Nobel Prize
careerModel.trajectory: Northern Irish farm boy -> poetry at Queen's University Belfast -> moved to Dublin -> Harvard and Oxford -> Nobel Prize 1995
careerModel.keyDecision: Refused inclusion in a British poetry anthology, insisting on his Irish identity
careerModel.scaleModel: Steady publication of poetry collections over decades, amplified by university positions and Nobel Prize
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about identity: refuse to be categorized by others, and let your work define where you belong

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote poems about bog bodies instead of slogans and made the Troubles bearable in print without ever softening them.

profiles.name: Mahmoud Darwish

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Poetry collections and cultural institutions
careerModel.trajectory: Born in village razed during Nakba -> internal exile in Israel -> joined PLO -> wrote the Palestinian Declaration of Independence -> most widely read Arab poet
careerModel.keyDecision: Used poetry as the vehicle for Palestinian identity when military resistance was failing
careerModel.scaleModel: Poetry that became a national identity, making the poet inseparable from the cause
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about justice: art can carry a cause further than politics when it speaks to the heart

profiles.oneLiner: Put a stateless nation into lines people could memorise and carry in their pockets.

profiles.name: Audre Lorde

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University teaching, book royalties, and grants
careerModel.trajectory: Librarian -> poet -> Hunter College professor -> defined intersectional feminism before the term existed -> New York State Poet Laureate
careerModel.keyDecision: Named all her identities simultaneously (Black, lesbian, feminist, mother, warrior, poet) when the world wanted her to pick one
careerModel.scaleModel: Essays and poetry that articulated what entire movements were trying to say
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about wholeness: refuse to pick one identity, and articulate the intersection others can't yet name

profiles.oneLiner: Refused to separate her identities into manageable portions and made that refusal a public method.

profiles.name: Nina Simone

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Live performance, recordings, and licensing
careerModel.trajectory: Classical piano prodigy -> rejected by Curtis Institute -> became nightclub singer -> 'Mississippi Goddam' made her a protest icon -> exile in Europe -> legacy grew after death
careerModel.keyDecision: Turned her rage at Curtis Institute's rejection and racial violence into protest music that defined an era
careerModel.scaleModel: Live performance and recordings that became more valuable with each decade, especially posthumously
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about justice: channel your rage into art, because protest music outlives protest marches

profiles.oneLiner: Turned a conservatory rejection into a protest career that changed what music could say.

profiles.name: Mercedes Sosa

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Concert performances and album sales
careerModel.trajectory: Argentine folk singer -> central to nuevo cancionero movement -> arrested on stage in 1979 -> exile in Paris and Madrid -> triumphant return
careerModel.keyDecision: Continued performing protest music despite arrest and forced exile, never compromising her art
careerModel.scaleModel: Voice of a continent's conscience, returning from exile to fill the largest stadiums in South America
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about your people: exile can be a chapter, not an ending, and your return will be more powerful than your departure

profiles.oneLiner: Gave a continent songs it could sing together when it couldn't otherwise agree on anything.

profiles.name: Fela Kuti

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Live performances and album sales
careerModel.trajectory: Nigerian musician -> studied in London -> created Afrobeat by fusing jazz, funk, highlife, and Yoruba percussion -> used music as political weapon against military governments
careerModel.keyDecision: Invented an entirely new genre (Afrobeat) to carry his political message, making the medium the movement
careerModel.scaleModel: Created a genre, a nightclub (the Shrine), and a commune, making his life the art form
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about resistance: invent the form that carries your message, because borrowed genres won't hold your truth

profiles.oneLiner: Built a song as a political building and dared the army to burn it down, which they did.

profiles.name: Miriam Makeba

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Concert performances and recordings
careerModel.trajectory: South African singer -> testified at UN against apartheid -> citizenship revoked -> 31 years of exile -> returned after apartheid fell -> 'Mama Africa'
careerModel.keyDecision: Testified at the United Nations against apartheid, knowing it would cost her citizenship and exile
careerModel.scaleModel: Music as cultural diplomacy, using international fame to keep apartheid in global consciousness
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about your country: use your art to keep the world watching, even when it costs you everything

profiles.oneLiner: Testified at the UN, lost her country, and sang the next thirty years on nine passports.

profiles.name: Maya Angelou

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties, speaking fees, and university position
careerModel.trajectory: Childhood trauma -> dancer, singer, activist -> I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings at 41 -> presidential inauguration poet -> Wake Forest professor -> national treasure
careerModel.keyDecision: Published her deeply personal autobiography at 41, when memoirs by Black women were nearly unheard of
careerModel.scaleModel: Personal testimony as literature, building a career from vulnerability that became universal
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about truth: your hardest story is the one that will reach the most people, so tell it fully

profiles.oneLiner: Was mute for almost five years as a child and then became the person American presidents asked to speak on their behalf.

profiles.name: Frida Kahlo

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Painting sales and commissions
careerModel.trajectory: Catastrophic bus accident at 18 -> painted from hospital bed -> almost entirely self-portraiture -> married Diego Rivera -> modest recognition in lifetime -> global icon posthumously
careerModel.keyDecision: Made her pain and body the subject of her art, turning personal suffering into universal expression
careerModel.scaleModel: Autobiographical art that became more valuable with each decade after death, fueled by feminist rediscovery
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about honesty: paint your own pain, because authentic self-expression compounds in value over time

profiles.oneLiner: Painted her own body from inside it and made self-portraiture carry the political weight of a mural.

profiles.name: Hilma af Klint

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Conventional portrait commissions funded secret abstract work
careerModel.trajectory: Trained Swedish painter -> produced first abstract paintings in 1906 (before Kandinsky) -> hid the work -> specified it remain hidden for 20 years after her death -> discovered and exhibited decades later
careerModel.keyDecision: Hid her most important work, trusting that the future would understand what her present could not
careerModel.scaleModel: Posthumous recognition after deliberate concealment, proving some work is ahead of its time
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about the work itself: make the art the world isn't ready for, and trust that the future will catch up

profiles.oneLiner: Invented abstract art in a side room nobody was watching, then locked the door for 40 years.

profiles.name: Louise Bourgeois

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Gallery sales and museum commissions
careerModel.trajectory: French-American sculptor -> autobiographical work for 70 years -> breakthrough MoMA retrospective at age 70 -> one of the most important sculptors of the 20th century
careerModel.keyDecision: Kept making autobiographical work for 70 years without major recognition, until MoMA gave her a retrospective at 70
careerModel.scaleModel: Seven decades of consistent work that compounded in recognition, with the breakthrough coming at 70
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about persistence: keep making the work for decades, because your breakthrough might come at 70

profiles.oneLiner: Waited until 70 for her retrospective and then worked for another 28 years at full intensity.

profiles.name: Akira Kurosawa

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Film direction and production
careerModel.trajectory: Painter -> assistant director -> Rashomon won Golden Lion at Venice -> first Japanese filmmaker to reach Western audiences -> 30 films across 57 years
careerModel.keyDecision: Submitted Rashomon to Venice Film Festival, opening Japanese cinema to the world
careerModel.scaleModel: One breakthrough film that opened an entire national cinema to international audiences
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about craft: enter the international competition, because one film can open the door for an entire culture

profiles.oneLiner: Turned every shot into a weather system and every film into a rehearsal for the next one.

profiles.name: Gabriel García Márquez

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and Nobel Prize
careerModel.trajectory: Colombian journalist -> wrote One Hundred Years of Solitude in 18 months of isolation -> 50 million copies sold -> Nobel Prize 1982 -> invented magical realism for the world
careerModel.keyDecision: Sold his car to support his family while writing One Hundred Years of Solitude in 18 months of isolation
careerModel.scaleModel: One novel that sold 50 million copies and defined an entire literary movement
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about place: write the story only you can tell about where you're from, and the world will recognize it as universal

profiles.oneLiner: Sold his car to buy eighteen months of writing time and came out of it with the defining novel of magical realism.

profiles.name: Georgia O'Keeffe

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Painting sales and gallery representation
careerModel.trajectory: Art teacher -> Alfred Stieglitz exhibited her work -> enlarged flowers and New Mexico landscapes -> moved to New Mexico permanently -> worked for 70+ years -> American art icon
careerModel.keyDecision: Moved permanently to New Mexico, letting the landscape become her entire visual vocabulary
careerModel.scaleModel: One distinctive visual language maintained for 70 years, becoming synonymous with American art
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about place: commit to one landscape and let it become your entire visual language

profiles.oneLiner: Painted one flower at the scale of a mural for fifty years and refused to let anyone call it erotic.

profiles.name: Chinua Achebe

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties, university positions, and cultural honors
careerModel.trajectory: Nigerian radio producer -> Things Fall Apart at 28 (20+ million copies) -> most translated African novel -> professor at Brown -> 'father of African literature'
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote Things Fall Apart in English to reach the colonizers' audience with an African story
careerModel.scaleModel: One debut novel that single-handedly created African literature as a global category
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about your culture: write in the colonizer's language to reach the widest audience, and redefine what that language can say

profiles.oneLiner: Built an English supple enough to carry Igbo proverbs and then used it to take Joseph Conrad to pieces.

profiles.name: Clarice Lispector

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and journalism
careerModel.trajectory: Ukrainian-born Brazilian -> published first novel at 23 -> diplomat's wife traveling the world -> returned to Rio and wrote prolifically -> recognized as one of the greatest writers in Portuguese
careerModel.keyDecision: Returned to Brazil and committed fully to writing after years as a diplomat's wife abroad
careerModel.scaleModel: Prolific output in one language that grew in international reputation over decades
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about interior life: write from the inside out, and trust that the specific becomes universal

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote in a Portuguese that had no precedent and made the language stretch to fit it.

profiles.name: Antoni Gaudí

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Architectural commissions, primarily from patrons
careerModel.trajectory: Catalan architect -> early patron Eusebi Guell -> took charge of Sagrada Familia in 1883 -> devoted final decade entirely to it -> died penniless -> building still under construction 100 years later
careerModel.keyDecision: Devoted his final decade entirely to the Sagrada Familia, living on-site as a pauper
careerModel.scaleModel: One unfinished building that became the most visited monument in Spain, funded by tourists and donations for 140+ years
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and care about transcendence: commit to the work that will outlive you, even if you never see it finished

profiles.oneLiner: Designed buildings by hanging weights from strings and then built them upside down in his head.

profiles.name: Charles and Ray Eames

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Furniture licensing royalties and design commissions
careerModel.trajectory: Married design partners -> Eames Office in Venice, California -> designed furniture, films, exhibitions -> Eames Lounge Chair still in production 70 years later
careerModel.keyDecision: Refused to separate furniture design from filmmaking, exhibitions, and architecture, treating all as one practice
careerModel.scaleModel: One design studio producing work across all media, with furniture royalties providing stable income
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and care about design: don't pick one medium, let all your interests feed each other, and let one product fund the exploration

profiles.oneLiner: Treated a chair, a house, and a film about the universe as the same design problem.

profiles.name: Gertrude Jekyll

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Garden design commissions and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Painter whose eyesight failed -> turned to garden design at 50 -> created 400+ gardens -> published 15 books -> became the most influential garden designer in English history
careerModel.keyDecision: Pivoted from painting to garden design when her eyesight failed, applying the same color theory to plants
careerModel.scaleModel: 400+ garden commissions combined with 15 books that taught the method to generations of designers
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about beauty: when one medium fails you, transfer your skills to another, and write about it so others can follow

profiles.oneLiner: Treated a flower bed as a piece of music with a start and an end and taught the whole Arts and Crafts movement to read the score.

profiles.name: Malcolm X

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Speaking fees and organizational support
careerModel.trajectory: Prison -> self-education -> Nation of Islam minister -> broke from NOI -> Hajj to Mecca transformed his worldview -> Organization of Afro-American Unity -> assassinated at 39
careerModel.keyDecision: Broke from the Nation of Islam and publicly revised his views after the Hajj, choosing truth over loyalty
careerModel.scaleModel: Oratorical power combined with autobiography that became one of the most influential books of the 20th century
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about growth: be willing to publicly revise your views when you learn new truth, even at great personal cost

profiles.oneLiner: Rebuilt his worldview in public, on camera, three times in twenty years.

profiles.name: Mahatma Gandhi

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Ashram community support and movement donations
careerModel.trajectory: London-trained lawyer -> South Africa for 21 years developing satyagraha -> returned to India -> led independence movement through nonviolent resistance -> independence 1947
careerModel.keyDecision: Developed satyagraha (truth-force) in South Africa as a method that could be replicated globally
careerModel.scaleModel: A replicable method of nonviolent resistance that could be taught and adopted by millions
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about justice: develop a method, not just a movement, so it can be used anywhere by anyone

profiles.oneLiner: Built a political method out of tiny, repeatable acts and ran it for forty years without revision.

profiles.name: Gloria Steinem

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Magazine publishing, books, and speaking
careerModel.trajectory: Journalist -> undercover at Playboy Club -> co-founded Ms. magazine in 1972 -> co-founded National Women's Political Caucus -> lifelong feminist organizer and speaker
careerModel.keyDecision: Co-founded Ms. magazine, creating a self-sustaining platform for feminist journalism
careerModel.scaleModel: Magazine as movement platform, with speaking and books amplifying the message
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about women's rights: build a media platform that sustains the movement financially

profiles.oneLiner: Went undercover to expose a single club and turned the byline into fifty years of organising.

profiles.name: Cesar Chavez

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Union dues and boycott movement support
careerModel.trajectory: Migrant farmworker -> community organizer -> co-founded National Farm Workers Association -> Delano grape strike and boycott -> first contracts for farmworkers
careerModel.keyDecision: Used consumer boycotts to give farmworkers leverage that strikes alone couldn't provide
careerModel.scaleModel: Consumer boycotts that gave powerless workers the economic leverage of millions of sympathetic shoppers
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about workers: connect the people with no power to the people with purchasing power

profiles.oneLiner: Built a union out of house meetings and turned a grape into a political question in American supermarkets.

profiles.name: Marie Curie

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University position and research grants
careerModel.trajectory: Polish immigrant to Paris -> studied physics -> discovered radium and polonium -> first woman Nobel Prize -> first person with two Nobels in different sciences
careerModel.keyDecision: Refused to patent the radium isolation process, insisting science should be freely shared
careerModel.scaleModel: Open science combined with relentless lab work that produced discoveries no one else could have made
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about discovery: share your methods freely, because your edge is your persistence, not your secrets

profiles.oneLiner: Processed a literal tonne of pitchblende in a leaking shed to isolate a tenth of a gram of radium.

profiles.name: Rosalind Franklin

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University research position
careerModel.trajectory: Chemist -> produced Photograph 51 showing DNA structure -> work used without credit by Watson and Crick -> died at 37 before Nobel Prize
careerModel.keyDecision: Insisted on careful experimental proof rather than premature model-building, producing the definitive image of DNA
careerModel.scaleModel: Meticulous experimental work that provided the foundation for one of the greatest discoveries in science
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about rigor: do the careful work even when others are racing ahead, and protect your data

profiles.oneLiner: Produced the image that unlocked DNA and was written out of its story for thirty years.

profiles.name: Barbara McClintock

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory research position
careerModel.trajectory: Cytogeneticist -> discovered jumping genes in maize in 1948 -> ignored for 30 years -> vindicated -> unshared Nobel Prize in 1983 at age 81
careerModel.keyDecision: Continued her research on transposable elements for 30 years despite the scientific community ignoring her findings
careerModel.scaleModel: Solitary research at one institution for decades, vindicated when the field finally caught up
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about truth: keep doing the work even when nobody listens, because vindication may take 30 years

profiles.oneLiner: Discovered jumping genes in the summer of 1944 and waited 35 years for the field to catch up.

profiles.name: Katherine Johnson

careerModel.primaryRevenue: NASA employment for 33 years
careerModel.trajectory: Math teacher -> joined NASA's predecessor in 1953 -> calculated Mercury, Gemini, and Apollo trajectories -> John Glenn refused to fly until she verified the computer's calculations
careerModel.keyDecision: John Glenn's insistence that she personally verify the computer's orbital calculations, proving human expertise alongside machine computation
careerModel.scaleModel: Essential contributions from within a large institution, recognized decades later through the film Hidden Figures
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and care about precision: do the work so well that the astronauts insist on you by name, even when the institution doesn't see you

profiles.oneLiner: John Glenn said he would not fly until she had checked the machine's numbers by hand.

profiles.name: Jane Goodall

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Research grants, books, and conservation organization
careerModel.trajectory: Secretary with no degree -> Louis Leakey sent her to Gombe in 1960 -> PhD from Cambridge without undergraduate degree -> 60+ years of chimpanzee research -> global conservation advocate
careerModel.keyDecision: Went to Gombe with no academic credentials, proving that patient observation mattered more than degrees
careerModel.scaleModel: 60 years of field research amplified by books and a conservation institute (JGI) with offices in 30+ countries
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about observation: go to the field with patience rather than credentials, and let decades of consistency build your authority

profiles.oneLiner: Sat still in a Tanzanian forest for sixty years until the chimpanzees started handing her the truth.

profiles.name: Rachel Carson

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and government salary
careerModel.trajectory: Marine biologist at US Bureau of Fisheries -> nature writer -> Silent Spring in 1962 -> launched the modern environmental movement -> died of cancer 2 years later
careerModel.keyDecision: Published Silent Spring despite chemical industry threats and personal illness, knowing it would transform policy
careerModel.scaleModel: One book that changed national policy, written by a government scientist who saw what industry was hiding
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about the environment: write the book the industry doesn't want published, because one book can change policy

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote a scientific book that started an environmental movement and did it while she was dying.

profiles.name: Aldo Leopold

careerModel.primaryRevenue: US Forest Service and university salary
careerModel.trajectory: Yale Forestry graduate -> US Forest Service -> helped create first wilderness area -> professor at University of Wisconsin -> A Sand County Almanac published posthumously -> foundation of environmental ethics
careerModel.keyDecision: Developed the 'land ethic,' arguing that humans are citizens of the biotic community, not its conquerors
careerModel.scaleModel: One posthumously published book that became the ethical foundation for modern environmentalism
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and care about land: write the ethical framework your movement needs, even if it's published after you're gone

profiles.oneLiner: Shot a wolf, watched the fierce green fire die in her eyes, and spent the rest of his life rebuilding his profession around the loss.

profiles.name: Anna Politkovskaya

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Newspaper salary and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Russian journalist at Novaya Gazeta -> reported on Chechen War and state violence -> assassinated on Putin's birthday in 2006
careerModel.keyDecision: Continued reporting on the Chechen War despite poisoning and direct threats, choosing truth over safety
careerModel.scaleModel: Fearless reporting from one newspaper that held power accountable until it cost her life
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about truth: some work is worth your life, but also build networks to protect other journalists after you

profiles.oneLiner: Reported on a war everyone else avoided until she was murdered on Putin's birthday.

profiles.name: Viktor Frankl

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Psychiatric practice, university positions, and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Austrian psychiatrist -> three years in concentration camps -> wrote Man's Search for Meaning -> founded logotherapy -> the book sold 16+ million copies
careerModel.keyDecision: Turned his Holocaust experience into a therapeutic framework (logotherapy) rather than just a memoir
careerModel.scaleModel: One book that sold 16+ million copies, combined with a therapeutic school taught worldwide
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about meaning: transform your worst experience into a framework that helps others find purpose in their suffering

profiles.oneLiner: Proved inside four concentration camps that the last human freedom is choosing one's attitude.

profiles.name: George Kennan
profiles.domain: US diplomacy and Cold War strategy

careerModel.primaryRevenue: State Department salary, then Institute for Advanced Study
careerModel.trajectory: Career diplomat -> wrote the Long Telegram from Moscow in 1946 -> architect of containment policy -> first director of Policy Planning Staff -> spent 50 years criticizing the policies his own work inspired
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote the Long Telegram, a single diplomatic cable that became the foundation of US Cold War strategy
careerModel.scaleModel: One document that shaped 50 years of foreign policy, written from within the government
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about strategy: one clear document written at the right moment can shape decades of policy

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote a 5,363-word telegram from Moscow that defined forty years of US foreign policy.

profiles.name: Frank Lloyd Wright

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Architectural commissions and Taliesin Fellowship fees
careerModel.trajectory: Apprenticed under Louis Sullivan -> 70-year career -> more than 1,000 designs -> founded Taliesin Fellowship as an apprentice program -> Fallingwater and Guggenheim as late-career masterpieces
careerModel.keyDecision: Founded the Taliesin Fellowship, turning his practice into an apprenticeship school that funded itself through student labor
careerModel.scaleModel: Apprenticeship model where students paid to learn while contributing to projects, sustaining the practice for decades
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about legacy: create an apprenticeship that trains the next generation while funding your practice

profiles.oneLiner: Turned apprenticeship into a commune and the commune into the labour force for Fallingwater and the Guggenheim.

profiles.name: Florence Nightingale

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Family wealth and government consulting
careerModel.trajectory: Upper-class Victorian woman -> Crimean War nursing superintendent -> used statistics to prove sanitation saves lives -> published Notes on Nursing -> founded modern nursing profession
careerModel.keyDecision: Used statistical analysis (pie charts of death causes) to convince the government to reform military hospitals
careerModel.scaleModel: Data-driven advocacy that changed policy, combined with a training school that professionalized nursing
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about health: use data to make your argument undeniable, then build the school that trains people in your method

profiles.oneLiner: Ran the numbers on dying soldiers and drew a pie chart that changed hospital hygiene forever.

profiles.name: Clara Barton

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Donations and government support for Red Cross operations
careerModel.trajectory: Teacher and patent clerk -> organized battlefield relief during Civil War -> founded American Red Cross in 1881 -> led disaster relief operations for 23 years
careerModel.keyDecision: Founded the American Red Cross at age 59, creating an institution that would outlast any individual effort
careerModel.scaleModel: National disaster relief organization with local chapters, scaling one person's impulse into an institution
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about crisis response: build the institution that can respond at scale, not just the individual effort

profiles.oneLiner: Built the American Red Cross out of her Washington apartment and ran it into the field until she was 79.

profiles.name: Jaime Escalante

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Public school teaching salary
careerModel.trajectory: Bolivian math teacher -> immigrated to US -> taught AP Calculus at Garfield High in East LA -> 14 students accused of cheating because nobody believed they could pass -> proved them all wrong
careerModel.keyDecision: Had his students retake the AP exam under surveillance to prove they hadn't cheated, turning accusation into triumph
careerModel.scaleModel: One classroom that proved poor students could excel at advanced math, inspiring the film Stand and Deliver
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about potential: believe in students nobody else believes in, and the results will speak for themselves

profiles.oneLiner: Taught calculus to kids nobody expected to sit the exam, by the sheer arithmetic of how many hours he was willing to stay in the room.

profiles.name: Marva Collins

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Private school tuition and speaking fees
careerModel.trajectory: Chicago public school teacher -> used $5,000 of her pension to open Westside Prep in her brownstone in 1975 -> taught Shakespeare and Plato to children from poverty -> turned down Secretary of Education position twice
careerModel.keyDecision: Used her own pension to start a school rather than waiting for institutional support
careerModel.scaleModel: One school that proved the method, with speaking and books spreading the philosophy
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about expectations: bet your own money on your method, then let the results silence the critics

profiles.oneLiner: Believed a four-year-old could discuss Plato if an adult had the patience to ask.

profiles.name: Rita Pierson

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Teaching salary and teacher training consulting
careerModel.trajectory: 40-year classroom teacher -> teacher trainer -> 2013 TED talk 'Every Kid Needs a Champion' went viral months before her death
careerModel.keyDecision: Spent her career building relationships with students rather than optimizing test scores
careerModel.scaleModel: One viral TED talk that crystallized a 40-year teaching career into a message seen by millions
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about connection: your philosophy can reach millions through one talk if you've lived it for decades first

profiles.oneLiner: Put her whole philosophy of teaching inside the single word champion and refused to apologise for it.

profiles.name: James Stigler

careerModel.primaryRevenue: UCLA professorship and research grants
careerModel.trajectory: UCLA psychologist -> ran comparative video studies of math teaching across Japan, Germany, and US -> co-authored The Teaching Gap -> showed why American math instruction fails
careerModel.keyDecision: Used video analysis of actual classroom teaching rather than test scores to understand why some countries teach math better
careerModel.scaleModel: Comparative video research that changed how education researchers study teaching
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about improvement: study what great practitioners actually do, not what they say they do

profiles.oneLiner: Took cameras into ordinary classrooms and changed how educators talk about what good teaching looks like second by second.

profiles.name: Dan Hughes

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Clinical practice, training workshops, and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Clinical psychologist -> developed Dyadic Developmental Psychotherapy for children with complex trauma -> trained therapists worldwide -> Building the Bonds of Attachment
careerModel.keyDecision: Created a specific therapeutic method (DDP) for children with disrupted attachment, filling a gap no existing therapy addressed
careerModel.scaleModel: Clinical method trained through workshops worldwide, with books making the theory accessible
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about healing: create a named method for the specific problem nobody else is treating, then train others to use it

profiles.oneLiner: Built a therapy around staying curious about a raging child long enough for them to stop.

profiles.name: Donald Winnicott

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Hospital practice and psychoanalytic work
careerModel.trajectory: Pediatrician at Paddington Green -> saw 60,000+ mothers and babies -> gave 50+ BBC radio talks to parents -> coined 'good enough mother' and 'transitional object' -> one of the most accessible psychoanalysts
careerModel.keyDecision: Used BBC radio talks to make psychoanalytic ideas accessible to ordinary parents
careerModel.scaleModel: Clinical practice feeding BBC broadcasts that reached millions of parents with usable concepts
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about parenting: translate clinical wisdom into plain language for the public, because parents need it most and get it least

profiles.oneLiner: Spoke to anxious parents on the radio in a voice that suggested they were already doing better than they feared.

profiles.name: Tenzin Palmo

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Donations for Dongyu Gatsal Ling Nunnery and teaching
careerModel.trajectory: London librarian -> ordained as Tibetan Buddhist nun -> 12 years in solitary cave retreat at 13,000 feet -> founded nunnery for Himalayan women -> international teaching
careerModel.keyDecision: Spent 12 years in solitary retreat in a Himalayan cave, building the depth needed for her later teaching
careerModel.scaleModel: Extreme depth through retreat, then institutional building (nunnery) and global teaching
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about depth: invest years in solitary practice before trying to teach, and the authority will be unmistakable

profiles.oneLiner: Lived twelve years in a Himalayan cave, then came down to build a school. That was harder.

profiles.name: Joyce Banda

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Political career and women's empowerment organizations
careerModel.trajectory: Founded women's empowerment organizations -> entered politics -> became second female head of state in Africa after president's sudden death -> served as President of Malawi 2012-2014
careerModel.keyDecision: Built women's empowerment organizations before entering politics, creating a base of grassroots support
careerModel.scaleModel: Grassroots women's organizations as the foundation for political power
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about empowerment: build the organizations first, then the political power follows naturally

profiles.oneLiner: Ran women's literacy circles in Malawian villages for twenty years, then used the same cohort method to run a country.

profiles.name: Phil Jackson

careerModel.primaryRevenue: NBA coaching salary
careerModel.trajectory: NBA player -> assistant coach -> integrated Zen Buddhism and Lakota philosophy into coaching -> 11 NBA championships with Bulls and Lakers -> most championships of any coach
careerModel.keyDecision: Integrated Zen Buddhism and Lakota philosophy into NBA coaching, when everyone thought sports and spirituality didn't mix
careerModel.scaleModel: Spiritual framework applied to elite athletics, attracting the most talented players in the world
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about presence: bring your spiritual practice into your professional work, because integration beats compartmentalization

profiles.oneLiner: Built championship teams by sitting in silence with them until they stopped performing for him.

profiles.name: Pat Summitt

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University coaching salary and endorsements
careerModel.trajectory: Became head coach at Tennessee at 22 -> 1,098 wins (most in NCAA history at the time) -> 8 national championships -> every senior graduated -> coached with early-onset Alzheimer's diagnosis
careerModel.keyDecision: Made every player commit to graduating, proving that athletic excellence and academic achievement aren't trade-offs
careerModel.scaleModel: 100% graduation rate alongside the most wins in NCAA history, proving you don't have to choose
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about the whole person: refuse to accept the trade-off between excellence and integrity

profiles.oneLiner: Held eye contact until you knew exactly what you owed her.

profiles.name: Erin Gruwell

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Teaching salary, then Freedom Writers Foundation and books
careerModel.trajectory: Assigned 150 'unteachable' 14-year-olds -> had them read Anne Frank and write daily journals -> 100% graduated -> Freedom Writers Foundation -> film
careerModel.keyDecision: Had her students read Anne Frank and write their own stories, treating their lives as literature
careerModel.scaleModel: One classroom story that became a book and film, then a foundation replicating the method
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about 'unteachable' kids: give them mirrors (books) and journals, and their stories become the curriculum

profiles.oneLiner: Gave 150 kids a composition book each and let what they wrote in it become the curriculum.

profiles.name: Sebastian Junger

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Books, documentary filmmaking, and journalism
careerModel.trajectory: Journalist -> The Perfect Storm -> embedded with US soldiers in Afghanistan -> Restrepo documentary -> founded Vets Town Hall -> veteran connection advocate
careerModel.keyDecision: Founded Vets Town Hall after realizing veterans needed community connection, not just therapy
careerModel.scaleModel: Books and documentaries that built credibility, then institutional work (Vets Town Hall) addressing the root problem
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about belonging: use storytelling to build credibility, then create the institution that solves the real problem

profiles.oneLiner: Believes most veterans are not suffering from war but from coming home alone, and designed a town hall ritual around that.

profiles.name: Hans Rosling

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Karolinska Institute professorship and Gapminder Foundation
careerModel.trajectory: Swedish public health physician -> co-founded Gapminder -> 2006 TED talk with animated bubble charts -> made global health data entertaining -> Factfulness bestseller published posthumously
careerModel.keyDecision: Used animated bubble charts in TED talks to make global health data entertaining and shareable
careerModel.scaleModel: Free data tools (Gapminder) plus viral presentations that changed how millions understand the world
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about truth: make data beautiful and entertaining, because facts only travel when they're fun to watch

profiles.oneLiner: Turned UN statistics into moving bubbles and stood in front of them like a sports commentator calling the race for human progress.

profiles.name: Mary Roach

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and magazine writing
careerModel.trajectory: Freelance journalist -> embedded with researchers for immersive science books -> Stiff, Bonk, Gulp, Grunt, Fuzz -> one of the most successful science writers in America
careerModel.keyDecision: Chose to embed with researchers and experience everything firsthand rather than reporting from a distance
careerModel.scaleModel: One deeply immersive book every few years on taboo or overlooked science topics, building a loyal readership
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about curiosity: go experience the thing yourself, because firsthand immersion makes better writing than interviews

profiles.oneLiner: Sticks her head inside whatever lab no one else wants to enter, then makes the reader laugh without making the scientist look silly.

profiles.name: Atul Gawande

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Surgery practice, New Yorker writing, and books
careerModel.trajectory: Surgeon -> New Yorker staff writer -> The Checklist Manifesto -> led WHO Safe Surgery initiative -> Being Mortal changed end-of-life conversations -> public health leader
careerModel.keyDecision: Published The Checklist Manifesto, turning a simple insight (checklists save lives) into global surgical policy
careerModel.scaleModel: Clinical practice feeding journalism that feeds policy change, each reinforcing the others
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about systems: find the simple intervention everyone overlooks, then write about it so compellingly that institutions adopt it

profiles.oneLiner: Took the hospital checklist that pilots take for granted and spent a decade proving it halved deaths in operating rooms around the world.

profiles.name: Neil deGrasse Tyson

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Hayden Planetarium directorship, TV production, and books
careerModel.trajectory: Astrophysicist -> director of Hayden Planetarium -> hosted Cosmos reboot -> StarTalk podcast -> most recognizable scientist in America
careerModel.keyDecision: Accepted the Hayden Planetarium directorship, choosing public science communication over pure research
careerModel.scaleModel: Institutional platform (Hayden) plus media presence across TV, podcast, and social media
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about excitement: choose the public-facing role even when peers value the lab, and use every medium available

profiles.oneLiner: Treats every question about the universe as a chance to show someone their own curiosity looks like everyone else's.

profiles.name: Steven Pinker

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Harvard professorship and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: MIT linguist -> The Language Instinct -> Harvard -> The Better Angels of Our Nature -> Enlightenment Now -> public intellectual for reason and progress
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote The Better Angels of Our Nature, using data to argue that violence has declined, against popular perception
careerModel.scaleModel: Big-idea books at 3-5 year intervals that shape public debate, backed by academic credibility
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about progress: use data to challenge popular pessimism, and write books big enough to shift the conversation

profiles.oneLiner: Writes academic books like popular books and popular books like academic books, and insists that is the point.

profiles.name: Sal Khan

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Philanthropy and grants
careerModel.trajectory: Hedge fund analyst -> free YouTube tutorials for cousin -> Khan Academy nonprofit -> philanthropic funding at scale -> free education for anyone, anywhere
careerModel.keyDecision: Turned down acquisition offers to keep Khan Academy free, choosing mission over wealth
careerModel.scaleModel: Free content at massive scale, funded by philanthropy from Gates Foundation and others
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about access: build free content first, prove demand, then fund via philanthropy

profiles.oneLiner: Recorded lessons for his cousin on a dollar Wacom tablet and refused to sell the result when offered millions for it.

profiles.name: Marcus du Sautoy

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Oxford professorship and broadcasting
careerModel.trajectory: Mathematician -> Simonyi Professor for Public Understanding of Science at Oxford -> popular math books and TV shows -> succeeded Richard Dawkins in the public science role
careerModel.keyDecision: Took the public understanding role, dedicating his career to making mathematics accessible
careerModel.scaleModel: University chair specifically for public engagement, combined with books and television
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about mystery: make the abstract beautiful, and seek the institutional role that supports public engagement

profiles.oneLiner: Talks about prime numbers the way a cellist talks about Bach, and teaches mathematicians to do the same.

profiles.name: Randall Munroe

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and xkcd merchandise
careerModel.trajectory: NASA roboticist -> started xkcd webcomic in 2005 -> What If? book series -> Thing Explainer -> full-time cartoonist and science explainer
careerModel.keyDecision: Left NASA to draw comics full-time, betting that his unique voice was more valuable than a stable career
careerModel.scaleModel: Free webcomic building audience, monetized through books and merchandise
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about fun: give the content away free, build an audience through consistency, then sell books to the fans who love you

profiles.oneLiner: Takes ridiculous questions seriously and serious questions ridiculously, until both yield physics you can draw as a stick figure.

profiles.name: Brian Cox

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University salary and BBC production fees
careerModel.trajectory: D:Ream keyboard player -> particle physicist at CERN -> BBC Wonders of the Solar System -> most popular science presenter in the UK
careerModel.keyDecision: Used his musician's sense of performance to make physics feel like a rock concert
careerModel.scaleModel: BBC partnership combining academic credibility with showmanship, plus live arena tours
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about wonder: bring your previous career's performance skills into science communication

profiles.oneLiner: Points at a desert horizon on camera as if it were proof of the universe and then does the maths to show it is.

profiles.name: Ruth Westheimer

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Radio, television, books, and speaking
careerModel.trajectory: Holocaust survivor -> Haganah sniper -> trained sex therapist -> 15-minute radio slot in 1980 -> became Dr. Ruth, America's sex therapist
careerModel.keyDecision: Talked openly about sex on radio when nobody else would, turning taboo into her competitive advantage
careerModel.scaleModel: Taboo topic + warm personality + media consistency = category of one
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about taboo topics: be the person willing to say what everyone is thinking, and warmth makes it safe

profiles.oneLiner: Spoke about sex in a grandmotherly German accent until an entire country agreed it was a normal thing adults could talk about.

profiles.name: Henry Louis Gates Jr.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Harvard professorship, PBS production, and books
careerModel.trajectory: Literary critic -> Harvard professor -> director of Hutchins Center -> host of Finding Your Roots on PBS -> made African American history mainstream television
careerModel.keyDecision: Created Finding Your Roots, using DNA and genealogy to tell individual stories that illuminate collective history
careerModel.scaleModel: Academic credibility powering a PBS franchise that makes history personal through genealogy
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about history: make it personal through individual stories, because people watch their own history

profiles.oneLiner: Treats DNA tests and slave ship manifests as instruments a living person can use to walk back into their own family.

profiles.name: Jacques Pepin

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Cookbooks, TV shows, and culinary education
careerModel.trajectory: Cooked for three French heads of state -> moved to US -> wrote La Technique -> TV cooking shows -> dean of culinary studies at International Culinary Center -> 80+ years of cooking
careerModel.keyDecision: Documented classical French technique in written and visual form, making it teachable to anyone
careerModel.scaleModel: Systematic documentation of technique through books and TV that created a curriculum anyone could follow
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about craft: document your technique so precisely that anyone can learn it, then teach it across every medium

profiles.oneLiner: Chops an onion on television the way a violinist plays an open string, not to impress but to show the next cook it can be done slowly.

profiles.name: Samin Nosrat

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and Netflix production
careerModel.trajectory: Apprenticed at Chez Panisse at 19 -> years of learning and teaching -> Salt Fat Acid Heat book and Netflix series -> made cooking principles accessible to a generation
careerModel.keyDecision: Reduced all cooking to four elements (salt, fat, acid, heat), making the complex feel simple
careerModel.scaleModel: One framework (4 elements) that organized an entire discipline, made visual through Netflix
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about simplicity: reduce your complex discipline to its essential elements, then illustrate them beautifully

profiles.oneLiner: Walked into Chez Panisse as a nineteen-year-old customer and did not leave the restaurant world until she had a framework that could teach home cooks without a recipe.

profiles.name: Ha-Joon Chang

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University salary and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: South Korean economist at Cambridge -> wrote Kicking Away the Ladder -> 23 Things They Don't Tell You About Capitalism -> made heterodox economics accessible to general readers
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote economics books for general readers that challenged mainstream orthodoxy with clear examples
careerModel.scaleModel: Academic credibility plus accessible writing that challenged economic orthodoxy for millions of readers
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about fairness: translate your field's hidden assumptions into language ordinary people can understand and challenge

profiles.oneLiner: Walks readers through the actual history of rich countries to show they did the opposite of what they now recommend to poor ones.

profiles.name: Eugenia Cheng

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University positions and popular math books
careerModel.trajectory: Category theorist -> Scientist in Residence at School of the Art Institute of Chicago -> How to Bake Pi -> made abstract math accessible through baking analogies
careerModel.keyDecision: Used baking analogies to explain category theory, connecting abstract math to everyday experience
careerModel.scaleModel: Popular books that use cooking metaphors to make the most abstract math feel approachable
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about abstraction: find the everyday metaphor that makes your expertise feel like common sense

profiles.oneLiner: Explains category theory by making a lasagna and insists the lasagna is not a metaphor.

profiles.name: Matthew Walker

careerModel.primaryRevenue: UC Berkeley professorship and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: British neuroscientist -> UC Berkeley sleep research center -> Why We Sleep became a massive bestseller -> changed how millions think about sleep
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote Why We Sleep for a mass audience, making sleep science feel urgent and personal
careerModel.scaleModel: One bestselling book that created a cultural shift in how people value sleep
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about health: write the one book that makes people feel the urgency of your research personally

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote a book on sleep that people refused to put down until morning, which he found darkly funny.

profiles.name: Siddhartha Mukherjee

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Columbia oncology position, books, and New Yorker writing
careerModel.trajectory: Indian-American oncologist at Columbia -> The Emperor of All Maladies won Pulitzer -> The Gene -> The Song of the Cell -> making medical science into narrative literature
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote the biography of cancer as narrative literature, not a medical textbook
careerModel.scaleModel: Medical practice feeding literary science writing that wins Pulitzers and reaches millions
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about disease: write the biography of the thing you're fighting, because narrative reaches further than data

profiles.oneLiner: Writes about cancer as a biography, the gene as a family story, and the cell as a building to be walked through room by room.

profiles.name: Mary Beard

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Cambridge professorship, BBC, and books
careerModel.trajectory: Cambridge classicist -> BBC presenter -> SPQR bestseller -> Women and Power -> made ancient Rome and feminist history mainstream
careerModel.keyDecision: Used social media and BBC to make classics public-facing, despite vicious online abuse
careerModel.scaleModel: Academic authority combined with accessible BBC presentation and social media engagement
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about the past: bring your expertise to the public through every medium, and don't let online abuse silence you

profiles.oneLiner: Shows up at Pompeii in a comfortable cardigan and argues with the audience about what a Roman slave actually thought about their emperor.

profiles.name: Trevor Noah

careerModel.primaryRevenue: TV hosting deal (The Daily Show) and touring
careerModel.trajectory: Born to illegal parents under apartheid -> stand-up in South Africa -> The Daily Show host -> Born a Crime bestseller -> global comedian and cultural translator
careerModel.keyDecision: Used his bicultural identity (Black mother, white father under apartheid) as the lens for all his comedy
careerModel.scaleModel: Personal identity as cultural bridge, scaled through late-night TV, books, and touring
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about bridging cultures: your in-between identity is the content, not a handicap to overcome

profiles.oneLiner: Grew up in multiple languages on the wrong side of apartheid law and turned that into a comedy voice American cable had never had.

profiles.name: Iain McGilchrist

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Writing and speaking fees
careerModel.trajectory: Oxford literary scholar -> retrained as psychiatrist -> The Master and His Emissary -> The Matter With Things -> argues the brain's hemispheres shape civilization
careerModel.keyDecision: Left literary scholarship to retrain as a psychiatrist, combining both perspectives in his hemispheric theory
careerModel.scaleModel: Paradigm-level books that bridge neuroscience and philosophy, building a following across disciplines
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about integration: retrain in another field entirely, then write the book that bridges both

profiles.oneLiner: Convinced that the left hemisphere is a brilliant assistant that has begun to act like the boss, and wrote two enormous books to say so slowly.

profiles.name: Karen Armstrong

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and speaking fees
careerModel.trajectory: Catholic nun for 7 years -> left convent -> struggled -> A History of God became bestseller -> TED Prize -> Charter for Compassion -> 25+ books on religion
careerModel.keyDecision: Used her TED Prize to create the Charter for Compassion, turning writing into a global movement
careerModel.scaleModel: Prolific writing on religion that crossed faith boundaries, amplified by TED platform
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about compassion: write across faith traditions rather than from within one, and use prizes as platforms for movements

profiles.oneLiner: Spent seven years in a convent, left without faith, and then spent forty more writing every major religion back into speaking terms with itself.

profiles.name: Robin Wall Kimmerer

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University salary, books, and speaking
careerModel.trajectory: Botanist and Citizen Potawatomi Nation member -> combined Indigenous knowledge with Western science -> Braiding Sweetgrass became a word-of-mouth phenomenon selling millions
careerModel.keyDecision: Braided Indigenous knowledge with Western botany in one book, when both communities told her to pick one
careerModel.scaleModel: Word-of-mouth bestseller that grew slowly for years then exploded, driven by genuine reader love
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about the land: combine your traditions instead of choosing between them, and trust word-of-mouth to find your audience

profiles.oneLiner: Writes about plants in the grammar that lets a sugar maple be a someone rather than a something.

profiles.name: Jill Lepore

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Harvard professorship and New Yorker staff writer
careerModel.trajectory: Harvard historian -> New Yorker staff writer -> These Truths (single-volume American history) -> one of the rare academics who writes for both scholarly and popular audiences
careerModel.keyDecision: Became a New Yorker staff writer while maintaining her Harvard position, bridging academic and public history
careerModel.scaleModel: Dual academic/journalism career that feeds both audiences and gives each credibility
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about history: write for both the academy and the public, because each audience makes the other trust you more

profiles.oneLiner: Writes American history the way a reporter writes a feature, down to the colour of the wallpaper, because she thinks the wallpaper tells you what the country was afraid of.

profiles.name: Yuval Noah Harari

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties from Sapiens trilogy
careerModel.trajectory: Hebrew University historian -> Sapiens (Hebrew 2011, English 2014) -> global bestseller -> Homo Deus -> 21 Lessons -> one of the most read historians alive
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote Sapiens as a narrative synthesis rather than original research, making history feel like a page-turner
careerModel.scaleModel: One breakthrough book that sold 25+ million copies, then leveraged into a platform and media company
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about the big picture: synthesize existing knowledge into a compelling narrative, because most people need the story, not the footnotes

profiles.oneLiner: Thinks 200,000 years of human history fit into 400 pages because silence has taught him to skip everything that was only opinion.

profiles.name: Michael Pollan

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and university positions
careerModel.trajectory: Journalist -> The Botany of Desire -> The Omnivore's Dilemma -> In Defense of Food -> changed how Americans think about food and later psychedelics
careerModel.keyDecision: Reduced his food philosophy to seven words: 'Eat food. Not too much. Mostly plants.'
careerModel.scaleModel: Cultural-moment books at 3-4 year intervals, each reframing a major topic (food, cooking, psychedelics)
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about food systems: distill complex systems into memorable maxims that change daily behavior

profiles.oneLiner: Follows a meal backward from the plate to the field and forward from the seed to the mind.

profiles.name: Rebecca Solnit

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and magazine writing
careerModel.trajectory: San Francisco essayist -> A Field Guide to Getting Lost -> Men Explain Things to Me coined 'mansplaining' -> 20+ books -> one of the most influential essayists in America
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote Men Explain Things to Me, giving a name to an experience millions of women recognized but couldn't articulate
careerModel.scaleModel: Essays that name unnamed experiences, creating vocabulary that enters the culture
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about naming: give language to the experience everyone recognizes but nobody has words for

profiles.oneLiner: Writes long essays that wander like walks, then deliver a single sentence you end up repeating to yourself for a decade.

profiles.name: Timothy Snyder

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Yale professorship and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Yale historian -> Bloodlands -> On Tyranny (sold millions post-2016) -> became public voice warning about authoritarianism -> Substack
careerModel.keyDecision: Published On Tyranny as a pocket-sized guide to resisting authoritarianism, making academic knowledge actionable
careerModel.scaleModel: Academic expertise made pocket-sized and actionable at the moment the public needed it most
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about democracy: distill your expertise into the smallest possible format at the moment of greatest need

profiles.oneLiner: Writes about tyranny the way a doctor writes discharge instructions: 20 lessons, each short, each testable at home.

profiles.name: David Graeber

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Academic positions and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Yale anthropologist -> fired (allegedly for politics) -> LSE professor -> Debt: The First 5,000 Years -> Bullshit Jobs -> helped inspire Occupy Wall Street -> The Dawn of Everything with David Wengrow
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote Debt reframing 5,000 years of economics as anthropology, challenging fundamental assumptions about money
careerModel.scaleModel: Academic books that became cultural touchstones by questioning assumptions everyone else accepts
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about questioning: challenge the most basic assumptions in your field, because the books that rewrite fundamentals reach the widest audience

profiles.oneLiner: Asked whether the thing everyone said was obviously true had ever actually been true, and then wrote the 500 pages it took to answer no.

profiles.name: Elaine Pagels

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Princeton professorship and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Historian at Princeton -> The Gnostic Gospels reframed early Christianity -> National Book Award -> combined personal grief with scholarship in later books
careerModel.keyDecision: Took the Nag Hammadi texts seriously as historical evidence when the field dismissed them as heresy
careerModel.scaleModel: Academic reframing of familiar material (Christianity) that reached a massive popular audience
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about hidden stories: take the dismissed texts seriously, because reframing the familiar is more powerful than discovering the new

profiles.oneLiner: Reads suppressed documents alongside the official ones and asks why the church needed the suppression.

profiles.name: Zadie Smith

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book advances, royalties, and NYU teaching
careerModel.trajectory: Wrote White Teeth as an undergraduate at Cambridge -> instant literary celebrity at 25 -> NYU professor -> novels and essays exploring multicultural identity in London and New York
careerModel.keyDecision: Published White Teeth at 25, then deliberately slowed down to develop as a writer rather than capitalizing on early fame
careerModel.scaleModel: Early breakthrough novel combined with sustained literary output and prestigious university position
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about depth: if fame comes early, slow down and develop your craft rather than rushing to capitalize

profiles.oneLiner: Writes the same postcode from fifteen angles until one of them sounds like a novel.

profiles.name: Lech Wałęsa

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Shipyard electrician salary, then presidential salary and speaking
careerModel.trajectory: Electrician at Lenin Shipyard -> led Solidarity, first independent trade union in a Communist country -> Nobel Peace Prize 1983 -> first freely elected president of Poland
careerModel.keyDecision: Led the formation of Solidarity inside a Warsaw Pact country, knowing it could mean prison or death
careerModel.scaleModel: Trade union as democracy movement, proving workers' organizing could topple a political system
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about freedom: organizing at work can become political revolution when the moment is right

profiles.oneLiner: Climbed a fence and turned a local wage strike into a ten-million-member political instrument.

profiles.name: Krista Tippett

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Public radio production and nonprofit revenue
careerModel.trajectory: Former diplomat -> created Speaking of Faith (now On Being) on public radio in 2001 -> built it into one of the most popular podcasts in the world
careerModel.keyDecision: Created a radio show about meaning and spirituality when media was moving away from those topics
careerModel.scaleModel: Long-form interview show that grew from radio to one of the most downloaded podcasts through depth, not trending topics
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about meaning: create the show nobody else is making, and let depth be your differentiator in an attention economy

profiles.oneLiner: Asks one more question than most interviewers think they are allowed to, and then waits.

profiles.name: John Hume

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Political salaries and Nobel Prize
careerModel.trajectory: Teacher -> civil rights organizer -> founded SDLP -> architect of the Good Friday Agreement -> Nobel Peace Prize 1998 with David Trimble
careerModel.keyDecision: Secretly engaged with Gerry Adams and the IRA when doing so was politically suicidal, because peace required talking to everyone
careerModel.scaleModel: Back-channel diplomacy and persistent dialogue across enemy lines over decades
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about peace: talk to the people your allies tell you not to, because peace requires everyone at the table

profiles.oneLiner: Held the same three sentences about non-violence for thirty years until the other side agreed to use them too.

profiles.name: Martti Ahtisaari

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Government salary and UN positions, then CMI foundation
