careerModel.trajectory: Finnish diplomat -> oversaw Namibian independence -> mediated Kosovo -> brokered Helsinki Accord ending Aceh insurgency -> founded Crisis Management Initiative -> Nobel Peace Prize 2008
careerModel.keyDecision: Founded Crisis Management Initiative after leaving office, institutionalizing his mediation expertise
careerModel.scaleModel: Government career building expertise, then a foundation that continued the work independently
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about peace: build the institution that continues your work after you leave office

profiles.oneLiner: Treated peace negotiations as a professional craft with a schedule and a room, not a moral occasion.

profiles.name: Tawakkol Karman

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Journalism and activism supported by international recognition
careerModel.trajectory: Yemeni journalist -> co-founded Women Journalists Without Chains -> led protests during 2011 Yemeni uprising -> youngest Nobel Peace Prize laureate at the time
careerModel.keyDecision: Led student-centered protests at Change Square despite extreme danger as a woman in Yemen
careerModel.scaleModel: Journalism as activism, amplified by international recognition that provided protection
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about freedom: use journalism as your shield and your weapon simultaneously

profiles.oneLiner: Ran the same weekly sit-in for three years before a revolution arrived to join her.

profiles.name: Tarana Burke

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Nonprofit organizations and speaking fees
careerModel.trajectory: Bronx activist -> founded Just Be Inc. in 2003 -> created Me Too in 2006 for young Black women survivors -> phrase went viral globally in 2017 -> navigated movement she started being credited to others
careerModel.keyDecision: Created Me Too as a grassroots program for Black women survivors 11 years before it went viral
careerModel.scaleModel: Grassroots movement that went viral through cultural moment, requiring its founder to reclaim and redirect it
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about survivors: start the work in your own community first, and if it goes viral, fight to keep its original purpose

profiles.oneLiner: Built a support practice in Alabama basements for a decade before the hashtag found it.

profiles.name: Ta-Nehisi Coates

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Magazine writing, book royalties, and MacArthur Fellowship
careerModel.trajectory: College dropout -> Atlantic senior writer -> The Case for Reparations -> Between the World and Me -> MacArthur Fellow -> wrote Black Panther for Marvel
careerModel.keyDecision: Published The Case for Reparations as a cover story, reopening a policy debate the country had closed
careerModel.scaleModel: Long-form journalism that shifted national conversation, amplified by a personal letter format (Between the World and Me)
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about justice: write the essay that reopens the debate everyone thought was settled

profiles.oneLiner: Writes sentences the way a boxer throws combinations, with the footwork done in the research.

profiles.name: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and speaking fees
careerModel.trajectory: Nigerian novelist -> Purple Hibiscus -> Americanah -> We Should All Be Feminists TED talk (sampled by Beyonce) -> one of the most influential African writers alive
careerModel.keyDecision: Her TED talk 'We Should All Be Feminists' reached millions when Beyonce sampled it, bridging literature and pop culture
careerModel.scaleModel: Literary fiction amplified by TED talks that reach a completely different audience
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about representation: give a TED talk that crystallizes your novels' themes, because it will reach people who never read literary fiction

profiles.oneLiner: Insists that the smallest unit of a story is not a country, it is one specific woman at a kitchen table.

profiles.name: Patti Smith

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Album sales, touring, books, and art
careerModel.trajectory: Arrived in New York with nothing -> poet -> merged poetry with punk rock (Horses, 1975) -> Just Kids memoir won National Book Award -> elder statesperson of American art
careerModel.keyDecision: Merged poetry with rock music when both worlds said it couldn't be done, creating a new form
careerModel.scaleModel: Authenticity sustained over 50 years, with memoir writing adding a second career in her 60s
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about merging forms: combine the two things you love even when both communities resist, and write the memoir when you're ready

profiles.oneLiner: Treats a stage, a notebook, and a Polaroid camera as the same tool.

profiles.name: Wisława Szymborska

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Poetry publications and Nobel Prize
careerModel.trajectory: Polish poet in Krakow -> published fewer than 350 poems across 50+ years -> Nobel Prize 1996 -> distrusted fame and stayed in Krakow
careerModel.keyDecision: Published sparingly (fewer than 350 poems in 50 years), letting quality replace volume
careerModel.scaleModel: Extreme selectivity that made each poem precious, validated by Nobel Prize
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about craft: publish less, not more, and let each piece carry the weight of your standards

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote one good poem a year for fifty years and threw out the rest.

profiles.name: Aretha Franklin

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Recording contracts, touring, and licensing
careerModel.trajectory: Baptist minister's daughter -> signed to Columbia at 18 -> breakthrough Atlantic recordings in 1967 -> 'Respect' became anthem of civil rights and feminism -> Queen of Soul
careerModel.keyDecision: Moved from Columbia to Atlantic Records, where Jerry Wexler let her play piano and be herself
careerModel.scaleModel: Unmatched vocal talent combined with songs that became cultural anthems, generating income for 50+ years
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about authenticity: find the collaborator who lets you be yourself, because constraint was hiding your genius

profiles.oneLiner: Took other people's songs and rebuilt them from the piano bench up until they belonged to her.

profiles.name: Luciano Pavarotti

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Opera performances, recordings, and concerts
careerModel.trajectory: Elementary school teacher who studied voice -> operatic debut at 26 -> nine high Cs -> Three Tenors -> made opera mainstream through stadium concerts and TV
careerModel.keyDecision: Performed in stadiums and on TV, bringing opera to millions who would never enter an opera house
careerModel.scaleModel: Elite craft made popular through accessible venues (stadiums, TV), massively expanding the audience
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about access: take your high art to the biggest venues possible, because the people deserve to hear it

profiles.oneLiner: Never learned to read music and became the most famous tenor of the twentieth century.

profiles.name: Tupac Shakur

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Album sales, acting, and posthumous releases
careerModel.trajectory: Born to a Black Panther -> poverty and instability -> five studio albums in four years -> murdered at 25 -> became one of the most influential rappers in history with massive posthumous catalog
careerModel.keyDecision: Recorded prolifically (five albums plus hundreds of unreleased tracks in four years), ensuring his voice would outlast his life
careerModel.scaleModel: Prolific recording created a massive catalog that generated revenue for decades after death
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about legacy: create volume alongside quality, because you never know how much time you have

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote like a prison correspondent and recorded like a man running a clock he could see.

profiles.name: Lin-Manuel Miranda

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Broadway production, film, and licensing revenue
careerModel.trajectory: Wrote In the Heights as a college sophomore -> Broadway -> Hamilton -> Disney's Moana and Encanto -> most influential musical theater creator of his generation
careerModel.keyDecision: Told the story of Alexander Hamilton through hip-hop, making the founding fathers feel contemporary
careerModel.scaleModel: One cultural phenomenon (Hamilton) that generated billions across Broadway, touring, film, and licensing
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about untold stories: use the genre nobody expects to tell the story everybody knows, and the collision creates something new

profiles.oneLiner: Turns biography into counterpoint, three voices at a time.

profiles.name: Ira Glass

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Public radio production and podcast revenue
careerModel.trajectory: 17 years as NPR production assistant -> created This American Life in 1995 -> pioneered narrative journalism on radio -> spawned Serial and an entire narrative podcast industry
careerModel.keyDecision: Spent 17 years learning his craft at NPR before creating his own show, letting the apprenticeship be the preparation
careerModel.scaleModel: One show that invented a genre (narrative podcast), then spawned an entire industry
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about stories: spend a decade or more learning your craft before launching your own platform, and the mastery will show

profiles.oneLiner: Turned a specific editing rule, get in the story fast and quote the person in scene, into a whole public radio house style.

profiles.name: Kae Tempest

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Live performance, albums, and books
careerModel.trajectory: South-east London spoken word performer -> youngest Ted Hughes Award winner -> Mercury Prize nominated albums -> novels and plays -> cross-genre artist
careerModel.keyDecision: Refused to choose between poetry, music, novels, and playwriting, making the refusal itself the artistic statement
careerModel.scaleModel: Multi-genre practice where each form feeds the others, with live performance as the anchor
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about expression: refuse to pick one medium, because the energy between forms is where your originality lives

profiles.oneLiner: Walks on stage and reads the room back to itself until it stops being separate rooms.

profiles.name: Wong Kar-wai

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Film production and distribution
careerModel.trajectory: Hong Kong filmmaker born in Shanghai -> works without completed scripts -> Chungking Express, In the Mood for Love -> Best Director at Cannes -> defined a visual and emotional language for loss and longing
careerModel.keyDecision: Worked without completed scripts, allowing the film to discover itself during production
careerModel.scaleModel: Auteur filmmaking where the process creates the art, valued by international festival and art-house circuits
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about emotion: trust the process over the plan, because the best work often emerges from uncertainty

profiles.oneLiner: Shoots until the actors forget they are acting, then edits until one year fits into one glance.

profiles.name: Hayao Miyazaki

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Animated film production and distribution (Studio Ghibli)
careerModel.trajectory: Animator -> co-founded Studio Ghibli -> My Neighbor Totoro, Princess Mononoke, Spirited Away (first anime Oscar) -> repeatedly 'retired' then returned -> The Boy and the Heron at 82
careerModel.keyDecision: Co-founded Studio Ghibli as an independent studio rather than working within the existing anime industry system
careerModel.scaleModel: Independent studio producing one masterpiece at a time, each hand-drawn, never compromising on craft
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about children: build your own studio where you control quality, and never automate what should be handmade

profiles.oneLiner: Draws the next frame by hand until he knows what the story is, and then draws it again.

profiles.name: Yayoi Kusama

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Gallery sales, museum exhibitions, and commissions
careerModel.trajectory: Japanese artist -> New York happenings scene 1958-1972 -> returned to Japan -> voluntarily lives in mental hospital since 1977 -> became one of the world's most popular living artists in her 80s and 90s
careerModel.keyDecision: Voluntarily checked into a mental hospital and continued creating art from there for 50+ years
careerModel.scaleModel: Immersive installations (Infinity Rooms) that generate social media virality and massive museum attendance
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about obsession: let your condition become your art form, because what makes you different is your competitive advantage

profiles.oneLiner: Treats the repeated mark as a survival technology and the repetition is the piece.

profiles.name: Björk

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Album sales, touring, and multimedia projects
careerModel.trajectory: Icelandic child recording artist -> Sugarcubes -> solo career from Debut through Fossora -> every album reinvents her sound completely -> multimedia art projects
careerModel.keyDecision: Reinvented her sound completely with every album rather than repeating what worked
careerModel.scaleModel: Constant reinvention that keeps a cult audience engaged for 30+ years, with multimedia expanding revenue
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about evolution: reinvent yourself completely with each project, and the audience that stays is the one worth keeping

profiles.oneLiner: Arrives at each album with a new set of instruments she has commissioned from other specialists.

profiles.name: William Kentridge

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Gallery sales, museum commissions, and opera direction
careerModel.trajectory: South African son of anti-apartheid lawyers -> developed charcoal animation technique (drawing, filming, erasing, redrawing) -> addressed apartheid's legacy -> major museum exhibitions worldwide
careerModel.keyDecision: Invented a drawing technique where erasure is visible in the final work, making history's disappearances literal
careerModel.scaleModel: Invented a unique medium that embodies his political themes, making the form inseparable from the content
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about history: invent the medium that makes your message physical, not just verbal

profiles.oneLiner: Erases most of a drawing back into its own smudge, and treats the smudge as memory.

profiles.name: Marcel Duchamp

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Art sales and patron support (minimal)
careerModel.trajectory: French painter -> Nude Descending a Staircase -> readymades (Fountain) -> publicly quit art for chess in 1923 -> secretly worked on Etant Donnes for 20 years -> reshaped the definition of art itself
careerModel.keyDecision: Submitted a urinal as art (Fountain, 1917), forcing the art world to question what art even is
careerModel.scaleModel: One provocative gesture that redefined an entire field, generating more discussion than any painting could
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about ideas: one gesture that reframes the question is worth more than a lifetime of answers

profiles.oneLiner: Proved that deciding is an art form by submitting a urinal and signing it R. Mutt.

profiles.name: Dieter Rams

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Braun design directorship and Vitsoe royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Braun chief of design for 34 years -> 606 Universal Shelving System (still in production) -> Ten Principles of Good Design -> influenced Jony Ive and Apple's design language
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote the Ten Principles of Good Design, codifying design philosophy that influenced an entire generation
careerModel.scaleModel: One design philosophy codified as principles, with products that stay in production for 60+ years
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about simplicity: codify your principles so clearly that they guide others for generations

profiles.oneLiner: Refused to make a product until he could answer the question, is it still useful in twenty years.

profiles.name: Massimo Vignelli

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Design studio fees from major corporate clients
careerModel.trajectory: Italian modernist -> co-founded Unimark International -> Vignelli Associates with wife Lella -> designed NYC subway map, IBM, Knoll identities -> champion of modernist design for 50 years
careerModel.keyDecision: Used only a handful of typefaces his entire career, proving that constraints create stronger work
careerModel.scaleModel: Consistent modernist philosophy applied to the world's biggest brands, creating a unified body of work
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about consistency: limit your toolkit drastically and let the constraints produce stronger work

profiles.oneLiner: Believed a designer's job is to refuse nine typefaces and use the tenth for forty years.

profiles.name: Tadao Ando

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Architectural commissions worldwide
careerModel.trajectory: Self-taught architect, former amateur boxer -> founded firm in 1968 -> Pritzker Prize 1995 -> known for exposed concrete, natural light, and spiritual spaces
careerModel.keyDecision: Never attended architecture school, teaching himself through travel and observation
careerModel.scaleModel: Self-taught mastery expressed through a signature material (concrete), attracting global commissions
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about self-education: you don't need the degree if you master your material through obsessive study

profiles.oneLiner: Pours a concrete wall smooth enough that sunlight draws the floor plan.

profiles.name: Paula Scher

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Pentagram partnership and design commissions
careerModel.trajectory: CBS Records art director (150 album covers/year) -> Pentagram partner since 1991 -> Public Theater identity -> Citibank -> 40+ years at the top of American graphic design
careerModel.keyDecision: Designed the Public Theater identity in a few minutes during a meeting, proving that decades of practice make speed possible
careerModel.scaleModel: Partnership model (Pentagram) that provides infrastructure while allowing individual creative autonomy
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about speed: invest decades in practice so that the right answer comes instantly when it matters

profiles.oneLiner: Treats typefaces as physical tools and is not shy about how much paint she wants on the brush.

profiles.name: Zaha Hadid

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Architectural commissions and awards
careerModel.trajectory: Iraqi-born, studied math in Beirut -> Architectural Association London -> first woman Pritzker Prize (2004) -> known for impossible-seeming parametric buildings -> died at 65
careerModel.keyDecision: Spent years as a 'paper architect' (unbuilt designs) before her first major building, proving ideas can build reputation before buildings do
careerModel.scaleModel: Visionary designs that built reputation through exhibitions and competitions before being built, creating demand for the 'impossible'
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about vision: share your ideas publicly even before they're built, because reputation precedes realization

profiles.oneLiner: Drew buildings the profession considered unbuildable until the profession built them.

profiles.name: Jan Gehl

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Urban consulting and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Danish architect -> wrote Life Between Buildings in 1971 -> 50 years studying how people use public spaces -> founded Gehl Architects -> transformed cities from Melbourne to New York
careerModel.keyDecision: Spent 50 years studying one thing (how people use public spaces) and refused to move on to other topics
careerModel.scaleModel: One area of deep expertise turned into a global consulting practice that transforms cities
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about people: study one question for your whole career, and cities will eventually come to you for answers

profiles.oneLiner: Counts people on a street the same way an ornithologist counts birds in a marsh.

profiles.name: Piet Oudolf

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Landscape design commissions
careerModel.trajectory: Dutch nurseryman -> pioneer of New Perennial Movement -> designed Lurie Garden, the High Line, and Serpentine Gallery garden -> changed how the world thinks about gardens
careerModel.keyDecision: Designed gardens that look beautiful in decay, not just in bloom, changing the definition of beauty in landscape design
careerModel.scaleModel: Signature approach (perennial plantings that are beautiful in every season) applied to the world's most prominent public spaces
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about beauty in all seasons: redefine what beauty means in your field, and the most prestigious commissions will follow

profiles.oneLiner: Designs for how a plant looks when it is dying as well as for how it looks in flower.

profiles.name: Malala Yousafzai

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Malala Fund donations, books, and speaking
careerModel.trajectory: Blogged for BBC Urdu at 11 under Taliban occupation -> shot by Taliban at 15 -> survived -> youngest Nobel Peace Prize laureate at 17 -> Oxford graduate -> Malala Fund
careerModel.keyDecision: Continued advocating for girls' education after being shot, turning personal tragedy into global platform
careerModel.scaleModel: Personal story of courage amplified by Nobel Prize and Malala Fund that invests in girls' education globally
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about education: your personal story of risk becomes the most powerful fundraising tool

profiles.oneLiner: Took the bullet that was meant to silence her and turned her recovery into a global fund.

profiles.name: Greta Thunberg

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and donations to climate organizations
careerModel.trajectory: Solo school strike at 15 -> catalyzed global Fridays for Future movement -> UN speeches -> became the face of youth climate activism
careerModel.keyDecision: Started a solo school strike, proving that one person's consistent action can catalyze a global movement
careerModel.scaleModel: One repeatable action (school strike) that anyone anywhere could copy, creating a leaderless global movement
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about the planet: design an action so simple that anyone can copy it, and consistency makes it impossible to ignore

profiles.oneLiner: Sat down outside the Swedish parliament alone and refused to leave until everyone else was also sitting down.

profiles.name: Al Gore

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Speaking fees, investments, and climate venture capital
careerModel.trajectory: Senator -> VP -> lost presidency in disputed election -> An Inconvenient Truth -> Nobel Peace Prize -> climate venture capitalist -> second act more impactful than the first
careerModel.keyDecision: Reinvented himself as a climate advocate after losing the presidency, turning defeat into a mission
careerModel.scaleModel: Documentary as persuasion at scale, combined with climate-focused investment fund
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about the climate: your biggest defeat can redirect you to your most important work

profiles.oneLiner: Took a losing presidential campaign and rebuilt his life around a single PowerPoint deck.

profiles.name: Dolores Huerta

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Union organizing and foundation work
careerModel.trajectory: Teacher -> co-founded National Farm Workers Association with Cesar Chavez -> lead negotiator during grape strike -> coined 'Si, se puede' -> still organizing in her 90s
careerModel.keyDecision: Became the lead negotiator for farm worker contracts, doing the detail work while Chavez did the public campaigning
careerModel.scaleModel: Complementary partnership where one partner campaigns publicly while the other negotiates the wins
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and care about workers: be the negotiator, not just the campaigner, because the contract is where change happens

profiles.oneLiner: Negotiated grape contracts for farmworkers in rooms where nobody expected a Mexican-American woman to sit at the table.

profiles.name: Naomi Klein

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties, journalism, and speaking
careerModel.trajectory: Canadian journalist -> No Logo at 29 -> The Shock Doctrine -> This Changes Everything -> 25 years of connecting capitalism, climate, and social movements
careerModel.keyDecision: Published No Logo in 1999, naming the anti-corporate globalization movement before it had language
careerModel.scaleModel: Big-idea books at 5-year intervals that name movements and provide frameworks for activism
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about power: write the book that gives the movement its vocabulary

profiles.oneLiner: Reads a crisis in the same week it is happening and files a book about it four years later.

profiles.name: Cédric Villani

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Academic positions, Fields Medal, and politics
careerModel.trajectory: French mathematician -> Fields Medal 2010 -> directed Institut Henri Poincare -> elected to French National Assembly -> tries to bridge math and public life
careerModel.keyDecision: Entered politics after winning the Fields Medal, trying to bring mathematical thinking to governance
careerModel.scaleModel: Academic fame leveraged into political influence and public engagement
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about public life: use your expertise as a platform for civic engagement, not just academic publishing

profiles.oneLiner: Treats a theorem as a piece of long-distance emotional weather that has to be survived collaboratively.

profiles.name: Susan Fowler

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Engineering salary, then writing and editorial work
careerModel.trajectory: Software engineer at Uber -> published blog post about systematic harassment -> catalyzed Uber CEO's departure -> Whistleblower memoir -> New York Times opinion editor
careerModel.keyDecision: Published 'Reflecting on One Very, Very Strange Year at Uber' on her personal blog, changing a company and an industry
careerModel.scaleModel: One blog post that catalyzed corporate accountability, combined with a personal platform that grew from the courage
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about accountability: one honest blog post can change an entire industry if you document everything carefully

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote a 3,000-word blog post that toppled a CEO from her own living room.

profiles.name: Cathy O'Neil

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Consulting, books, and speaking
careerModel.trajectory: Harvard math PhD -> Wall Street quant -> Occupy Wall Street activist -> wrote Weapons of Math Destruction -> founded algorithmic auditing consultancy ORCAA
careerModel.keyDecision: Left Wall Street for activism, then turned her math expertise into a new field (algorithmic auditing)
careerModel.scaleModel: Book that named a problem (algorithmic bias), then a consulting firm that solves it
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about fairness: name the problem your industry creates, then build the business that fixes it

profiles.oneLiner: Left a hedge fund to teach the public how to sue algorithms.

profiles.name: Hedy Lamarr

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Film salary (acting career)
careerModel.trajectory: Austrian actress -> fled arms-dealer husband -> MGM star -> co-invented frequency-hopping spread spectrum for torpedo guidance in WWII -> patent expired before technology was commercialized -> recognized decades later as WiFi/Bluetooth pioneer
careerModel.keyDecision: Co-invented frequency-hopping technology to help the Allied war effort, receiving no financial benefit
careerModel.scaleModel: Invention ahead of its time, recognized posthumously as foundational to modern wireless technology
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about contribution: protect your inventions legally, because ideas ahead of their time may be worth billions decades later

profiles.oneLiner: Patented the working principle of modern wireless on a kitchen table between film takes.

profiles.name: Pearl Kazin Bell

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Editorial positions at major publications
careerModel.trajectory: Harper's Bazaar -> The New Yorker copy editor -> fiction critic for The New Leader, Commentary, and Partisan Review -> shaped literary taste through editing rather than writing
careerModel.keyDecision: Chose to shape literature through editing and criticism rather than pursuing her own creative writing
careerModel.scaleModel: Curatorial influence across multiple prestigious publications over decades
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about literature: shaping other people's work can be your life's art form

profiles.oneLiner: Read fiction the way a watchmaker listens to a movement, then wrote down exactly what she heard.

profiles.name: Gordon Lish

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Editor positions at Esquire and Knopf, plus teaching
careerModel.trajectory: Fiction editor at Esquire -> editor at Knopf -> published Raymond Carver, Don DeLillo, Barry Hannah -> legendary writing workshops -> controversial for how heavily he edited Carver
careerModel.keyDecision: Edited Raymond Carver's stories so extensively that he essentially co-authored them, creating 'minimalism'
careerModel.scaleModel: Editorial power that shaped an entire literary movement (minimalism) through aggressive curation and editing
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about craft: great editing can be as creative as great writing, but always credit the artist

profiles.oneLiner: Taught writers that every sentence must earn the right to exist. The next one especially.

profiles.name: Herbert Kohl

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Teaching and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Sixth-grade teacher in Harlem -> wrote 36 Children (1967) -> founded Open Schools movement -> advocated for progressive education for 50+ years
careerModel.keyDecision: Published 36 Children, an honest account of teaching in Harlem that became a progressive education manifesto
careerModel.scaleModel: One classroom memoir that launched a movement, sustained by decades of writing and advocacy
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about honesty in education: write truthfully about your classroom, and the book becomes the manifesto

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote down what the children in Harlem actually said and let those sentences argue for a better school.

profiles.name: Rafe Esquith

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Teaching salary, books, and Hobart Shakespeareans program
careerModel.trajectory: Fifth-grade teacher at Hobart Elementary in LA for 31 years -> founded Hobart Shakespeareans with immigrant children from poverty -> taught Shakespeare, Plato, and rock band
careerModel.keyDecision: Had elementary school children perform full Shakespeare plays, proving that poverty doesn't limit potential
careerModel.scaleModel: One extraordinary classroom that attracted donations, book deals, and media attention for decades
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about raising the bar: set expectations absurdly high for students everyone has written off, and the results will speak

profiles.oneLiner: Ran a classroom at 6:30 in the morning where ten-year-olds rehearsed Macbeth and meant every word of it.

profiles.name: Richard Feynman

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Caltech professorship and Nobel Prize
careerModel.trajectory: Manhattan Project physicist -> Nobel Prize for quantum electrodynamics -> Feynman Lectures -> Challenger investigation -> made physics feel like play
careerModel.keyDecision: Recorded the Feynman Lectures on Physics, creating the most influential physics teaching resource in history
careerModel.scaleModel: Teaching as performance art that made physics accessible, amplified by books and one legendary investigation (Challenger O-ring demo)
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about play: treat your expertise as a game to be shared, not a credential to be guarded

profiles.oneLiner: Insisted that the first principle of science was that you must not fool yourself, and made the joke of physics feel like the point of it.

profiles.name: Jerome Bruner

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University positions at Harvard, Oxford, and NYU
careerModel.trajectory: Founder of cognitive revolution in psychology -> The Process of Education introduced spiral curriculum -> taught at Harvard, Oxford, and NYU for 70 years
careerModel.keyDecision: Introduced the spiral curriculum concept, arguing that any subject can be taught to any child at any age in some honest form
careerModel.scaleModel: One idea (spiral curriculum) that restructured education worldwide, backed by 70 years of academic credibility
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about how people learn: find the one structural idea that reorganizes your field, then spend your career proving it

profiles.oneLiner: Argued that any subject could be taught to any child at any stage, if you were honest about what the subject really was.

profiles.name: Harold McGee

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and consulting
careerModel.trajectory: English literature student -> wrote On Food and Cooking (1984) -> became the definitive reference on the science of cooking -> revised it 20 years later -> every serious chef owns it
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote the definitive reference on food science, filling a gap no one else had addressed
careerModel.scaleModel: One reference book so thorough that it became essential for an entire profession
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about being definitive: write the reference book your field doesn't have yet, and revise it as knowledge grows

profiles.oneLiner: Proved that a kitchen was the best-equipped laboratory most people would ever own, and wrote the manual for it.

profiles.name: Marcus Aurelius

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Roman emperor (state resources)
careerModel.trajectory: Adopted heir -> studied Stoic philosophy -> Roman emperor 161-180 CE -> wrote the Meditations as a private journal during military campaigns -> never intended them for publication -> one of the most read philosophy texts in history
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote the Meditations as a private practice for himself, not as a published work, which is why they feel so honest
careerModel.scaleModel: Private journaling that became one of history's most enduring philosophical texts precisely because it was never meant for an audience
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about self-improvement: write for yourself first, because the most honest writing finds its audience centuries later

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote a journal to himself on the northern frontier and accidentally left a manual for how to run a human being.

profiles.name: Epictetus

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Teaching at his school in Nicopolis
careerModel.trajectory: Born a slave in Phrygia -> freed as a young man -> taught in Rome -> banished by Domitian -> founded school in Nicopolis -> never wrote anything, but his student Arrian recorded his teachings
careerModel.keyDecision: Never wrote anything himself, trusting his teaching to be captured by students, which made his ideas feel more alive
careerModel.scaleModel: Oral teaching recorded by students that has endured for 2,000 years
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about wisdom: focus on the teaching, not the writing, and trust that someone will preserve what matters

profiles.oneLiner: Divided the world into what is yours and what is not, and refused to let his students confuse the two.

profiles.name: Tim Gowers

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Cambridge professorship and Fields Medal
careerModel.trajectory: Cambridge mathematician -> Fields Medal 1998 -> Mathematics: A Very Short Introduction -> pioneered Polymath Project for collaborative mathematical research
careerModel.keyDecision: Created the Polymath Project, applying open-source collaboration to mathematical research
careerModel.scaleModel: Open collaboration model that proved mathematics could be done collectively online
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about collaboration: apply open-source principles to your field, because collective intelligence outperforms solo genius

profiles.oneLiner: Opened his own thinking in public and invited any mathematician in the world to step in beside him.

profiles.name: George Steiner

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University positions and New Yorker criticism
careerModel.trajectory: Trilingual from childhood (English, French, German) -> Princeton, Cambridge, Geneva -> New Yorker critic -> explored what happens to language and culture after the Holocaust
careerModel.keyDecision: Used his trilingual background to work across literary traditions that most critics could only approach from one side
careerModel.scaleModel: Cross-cultural literary criticism that connected traditions most scholars treated separately
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about language: your multilingual or multicultural background is your intellectual edge, not a distraction

profiles.oneLiner: Argued that every act of understanding was already a translation, and that multilingual life was the only honest condition.

profiles.name: Edith Grossman

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Translation fees and royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Literary translator -> translated Garcia Marquez, Vargas Llosa, Cervantes -> her 2003 Don Quixote became the standard English translation -> proved translation is an art form
careerModel.keyDecision: Translated Don Quixote at age 67, producing the translation that replaced all previous versions
careerModel.scaleModel: Definitive translations of major literary works that generate royalties for decades
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about bridge-building: translation is creation, and the definitive version of a classic is a life's work

profiles.oneLiner: Held that fidelity in translation meant writing the second book, not tracing the first.

profiles.name: Gregory Rabassa

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Translation fees and university teaching
careerModel.trajectory: Translated Cortazar, Garcia Marquez, and the Latin American Boom into English -> Garcia Marquez said his translation was better than the original -> brought a literary movement to the English-speaking world
careerModel.keyDecision: Dedicated his career to translating Latin American literature, becoming the bridge for an entire literary movement
careerModel.scaleModel: Essential intermediary for a literary movement, making each author's work accessible to an English-speaking audience of millions
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about connection: be the bridge between two worlds, because both need you

profiles.oneLiner: Was paid in the original author's astonishment when García Márquez said the English was better than the Spanish.

profiles.name: Clifford Geertz

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University positions at Chicago and Institute for Advanced Study
careerModel.trajectory: Cultural anthropologist -> fieldwork in Indonesia and Morocco -> The Interpretation of Cultures (1973) -> 'thick description' became the method of a generation -> Institute for Advanced Study
careerModel.keyDecision: Introduced 'thick description' to anthropology, making interpretation rather than measurement the method
careerModel.scaleModel: One methodological concept that reorganized an entire discipline
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about understanding: name your method, because a named method travels further than unnamed practice

profiles.oneLiner: Renamed his discipline a branch of literature by insisting that what an anthropologist did was write thick description.

profiles.name: Bruno Latour

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Academic positions and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: French sociologist -> Laboratory Life (ethnography of Salk Institute) -> helped found science and technology studies -> We Have Never Been Modern -> Gaia lectures
careerModel.keyDecision: Applied ethnographic methods to a scientific laboratory, treating scientists like any other tribe
careerModel.scaleModel: Methodological provocation that created an entirely new field (science and technology studies)
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about hidden assumptions: study the powerful the way anthropologists study others, and the insights will create a new field

profiles.oneLiner: Treated scientists, microbes, doorknobs and courts as equally worthy of ethnographic attention.

profiles.name: Donella Meadows

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Academic work and Sustainability Institute
careerModel.trajectory: Environmental scientist -> lead author of The Limits to Growth (1972, Club of Rome) -> Thinking in Systems -> Donella Meadows Institute -> introduced systems modeling to millions
careerModel.keyDecision: Co-authored The Limits to Growth, making systems dynamics modeling accessible to the general public
careerModel.scaleModel: One report that changed global environmental conversation, followed by teaching materials that taught the method
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about systems: model the system so people can see where it's heading, because visualization is more persuasive than argument

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote the gentlest manual for how to notice a feedback loop, and then insisted the point was to dance with it, not control it.

profiles.name: Fritjof Capra

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Books and Center for Ecoliteracy
careerModel.trajectory: Austrian-born physicist -> The Tao of Physics (1975) drew parallels between physics and Eastern mysticism -> founded Center for Ecoliteracy -> systems thinking advocate for 50 years
careerModel.keyDecision: Connected modern physics with Eastern mysticism in The Tao of Physics, when both communities thought they had nothing in common
careerModel.scaleModel: Bridging two seemingly unrelated fields in one bestselling book, then building institutions around the synthesis
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about connection: find the unexpected parallel between two fields, because the bridge itself becomes your career

profiles.oneLiner: Held that the universe modern physics was uncovering looked more like the one the mystics described than the one Newton drew.

profiles.name: Mary Catherine Bateson

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University positions and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Daughter of Margaret Mead and Gregory Bateson -> anthropologist at Harvard, Amherst, George Mason -> Composing a Life showed how women improvise careers from interruptions
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote Composing a Life, reframing women's interrupted careers as creative improvisation rather than failure
careerModel.scaleModel: One book that reframed how women (and men) think about non-linear careers
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about interrupted careers: your zigzag path is a creative composition, not a failure to plan

profiles.oneLiner: Said that composing a life was improvisation, and that improvisation was a craft that took hours of practice like any other.

profiles.name: Mircea Eliade

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University of Chicago professorship
careerModel.trajectory: Romanian scholar -> studied in India -> exiled after WWII -> University of Chicago from 1957 until death -> The Sacred and the Profane -> mapped how all religions use space, time, and ritual
careerModel.keyDecision: Created a comparative framework for all religions that transcended any single tradition
careerModel.scaleModel: Comprehensive framework for understanding sacred experience across all cultures
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about patterns: build the framework that applies across all cases, not just the ones you know best

profiles.oneLiner: Argued that the sacred showed itself in ordinary objects, and built a method for noticing the moment it did.

profiles.name: David Bohm

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Academic positions (Brazil, Israel, UK)
careerModel.trajectory: Oppenheimer student -> blacklisted during McCarthy era -> worked in Brazil, Israel, then Birkbeck College London -> Wholeness and the Implicate Order -> developed Bohmian dialogue practice
careerModel.keyDecision: Developed dialogue practice as a method for collective thinking, bridging physics and human communication
careerModel.scaleModel: Theoretical physics combined with practical dialogue method used by organizations worldwide
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about collective thinking: develop a structured practice for group dialogue, because conversations need design as much as buildings do

profiles.oneLiner: Taught groups to sit together and suspend their assumptions until they could feel reality unfolding.

profiles.name: Gregory Bateson

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Academic positions and research grants
careerModel.trajectory: British anthropologist -> Bali fieldwork with Margaret Mead -> cybernetics -> Steps to an Ecology of Mind -> worked across anthropology, psychiatry, evolution, and epistemology
careerModel.keyDecision: Refused to stay in one field, working across anthropology, psychiatry, cybernetics, and ecology
careerModel.scaleModel: Cross-disciplinary thinking collected in one essay volume that became essential reading across multiple fields
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about systems: refuse to pick one discipline, and let the connections between fields be your contribution

profiles.oneLiner: Held that the major problems of the world came from the gap between how nature worked and how people thought.

profiles.name: Frances Yates

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Warburg Institute position and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: British historian at the Warburg Institute -> The Art of Memory and Giordano Bruno and the Hermetic Tradition -> revealed hidden intellectual traditions behind the Renaissance
careerModel.keyDecision: Took Renaissance hermeticism seriously as intellectual history when others dismissed it as superstition
careerModel.scaleModel: Deep scholarship on overlooked traditions that reframed how scholars understand the Renaissance
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about hidden knowledge: study the traditions your field dismisses, because they might be the key to understanding the whole picture

profiles.oneLiner: Rebuilt the mental palaces of Renaissance mnemonists so that twentieth-century readers could walk through them.

profiles.name: Martha Nussbaum

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University of Chicago professorship and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Harvard philosopher -> Chicago -> Capabilities Approach with Amartya Sen -> The Fragility of Goodness, Creating Capabilities -> one of the most influential living philosophers
careerModel.keyDecision: Developed the Capabilities Approach with Amartya Sen, making philosophy practical for development policy
careerModel.scaleModel: Philosophical framework adopted by UN and development agencies, proving philosophy can shape policy
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about human development: make your philosophy practical enough for policy makers to use

profiles.oneLiner: Argued that emotions were not the opposite of reason but a form of it, and rebuilt moral philosophy from that observation.

profiles.name: Myles Horton

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Highlander Folk School grants and donations
careerModel.trajectory: Founded Highlander Folk School in 1932 -> trained labor organizers in the 1930s-40s -> trained civil rights leaders (Rosa Parks, MLK) in the 1950s-60s -> Citizenship Schools
careerModel.keyDecision: Created Citizenship Schools that taught literacy as voter registration, connecting education to political power
careerModel.scaleModel: One training center that produced leaders for every major social movement of the 20th century
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and care about education: build the training center that serves every movement, not just one

profiles.oneLiner: Ran a school where the first principle was that poor people already knew the answers.

profiles.name: Paulo Freire

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University positions and book royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Brazilian educator -> exiled after 1964 coup -> wrote Pedagogy of the Oppressed in Chile -> 1 million+ copies -> returned to Brazil as Secretary of Education of Sao Paulo -> most cited education book in the world
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote Pedagogy of the Oppressed in exile, turning his expulsion into the time needed for his most important work
careerModel.scaleModel: One book written in exile that became the most cited education text in history, applied in every country
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about liberation: exile can give you the distance to write the work that changes everything

profiles.oneLiner: Refused to teach by depositing words. Built a method that began with what people already knew.

profiles.name: William Shakespeare

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Theater company shareholder and playwright
careerModel.trajectory: Stratford glover's son -> actor and playwright in London -> shareholder in Lord Chamberlain's Men/King's Men -> built the Globe -> 39 plays and 154 sonnets -> retired to Stratford wealthy
careerModel.keyDecision: Became a shareholder in his theater company rather than just a writer-for-hire, owning equity in his own work
careerModel.scaleModel: Ownership stake in the theater company that performed his work, aligning creation with financial upside
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about ownership: take equity in the platform that distributes your work, not just a fee for creating it

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote the soliloquy everyone recognises and the love sonnet every other has to answer to.

profiles.name: Rumi

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Community support and scholarly patronage
careerModel.trajectory: Islamic scholar in Konya -> met Shams-i-Tabrizi, a wandering mystic -> the encounter transformed him from scholar to poet -> 25,000-couplet Masnavi -> founded Mevlevi Order (whirling dervishes)
careerModel.keyDecision: Let one encounter with Shams destroy his previous identity as a conventional scholar, and wrote from the ruins
careerModel.scaleModel: Poetry so universal that 800 years later Rumi is the bestselling poet in America
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and care about transformation: let the encounter that destroys your old self become the source of your life's work

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote that there is a field out beyond right and wrong, and said he would meet you there.

profiles.name: Ursula K. Le Guin

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and teaching
careerModel.trajectory: Daughter of anthropologists -> wrote Earthsea and The Left Hand of Darkness -> used speculative fiction to explore gender, power, and anarchism -> National Book Foundation Medal -> 60+ years of writing
careerModel.keyDecision: Used science fiction and fantasy to explore social and political ideas that 'literary' fiction wouldn't touch
careerModel.scaleModel: Genre fiction as vehicle for radical ideas, building a readership that expected intellectual depth in fantasy
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about ideas: use genre fiction to explore the questions serious literature ignores, because the imagined world reveals the real one

profiles.oneLiner: Treated the sentence as a piece of music and the story as a sea voyage, and would not let her students forget either.

profiles.name: Haruki Murakami

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties from global translations
careerModel.trajectory: Ran a jazz bar in Tokyo until age 29 -> started writing during a baseball game -> Norwegian Wood made him famous -> runs marathons as creative practice -> global literary phenomenon
careerModel.keyDecision: Closed his jazz bar to write full-time, and used marathon running to sustain the physical discipline for daily writing
careerModel.scaleModel: Consistent daily writing practice sustained by physical discipline, producing novels translated into 50+ languages
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about discipline: find a physical practice (running, swimming, walking) that sustains your creative practice

profiles.oneLiner: Ran an hour a day, wrote a thousand words a day, and said the two practices were the same practice.

profiles.name: Octavia Butler

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and MacArthur Fellowship
careerModel.trajectory: Grew up poor in Pasadena -> wrote Kindred and Parable of the Sower -> first science fiction writer to receive MacArthur Genius Grant -> one of the most influential sci-fi writers ever
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote Black women as protagonists of science fiction when the genre had almost none, creating a new tradition
careerModel.scaleModel: Pioneering representation in genre fiction that created a new readership and inspired a generation of writers
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about representation: put your community at the center of the genre that excluded them

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote on the inside of a notebook in 1988 that she would be a bestselling writer, then spent the next eighteen years quietly making it true.

profiles.name: Toni Cade Bambara

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Writing, teaching, and community organizing
careerModel.trajectory: Writer and community activist -> Gorilla, My Love -> The Salt Eaters -> edited landmark Black women's anthologies -> moved to Philadelphia to do community video work
careerModel.keyDecision: Moved from literary New York to community-based video work in Philadelphia, choosing grassroots over prestige
careerModel.scaleModel: Literary reputation combined with community organizing, using each to fuel the other
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about community: move toward the grassroots, not the prestige, and let your art serve the neighborhood

profiles.oneLiner: Treated the writer as a cultural worker and the story as a rescue mission for a community's memory.

profiles.name: Philip Glass

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Commissions, recordings, and film scores
careerModel.trajectory: Studied in Paris with Nadia Boulanger -> drove a taxi and did plumbing while composing -> Einstein on the Beach -> Koyaanisqatsi -> hundreds of film scores and concert works -> central figure in minimalism
careerModel.keyDecision: Drove a taxi and did plumbing to fund his composing until he could support himself through music alone
careerModel.scaleModel: Day jobs funding art until the art could sustain itself, then prolific output across concert halls and film
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about independence: keep the day job that funds your art without draining it, and quantity enables quality

profiles.oneLiner: Drove a taxi and fixed sinks until he was 41 so that the music he wrote would not have to pay the rent.

profiles.name: Anni Albers

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Teaching, art sales, and commissions
careerModel.trajectory: Bauhaus student -> master weaver and teacher at Black Mountain College -> On Weaving became the most influential textile book -> 50+ years of treating weaving as a fine art
careerModel.keyDecision: Chose weaving as her medium at the Bauhaus when painting was reserved for men, then elevated it to fine art
careerModel.scaleModel: One medium (weaving) elevated from craft to art through decades of practice and one definitive book
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about craft: elevate your medium by doing it better than anyone and writing the definitive book about it

profiles.oneLiner: Treated thread as a medium with the same seriousness a painter gave to pigment, and asked her readers to remember how to touch.

profiles.name: Andrei Tarkovsky

careerModel.primaryRevenue: State film studio commissions (Soviet era), then European production
careerModel.trajectory: Soviet filmmaker -> Ivan's Childhood, Andrei Rublev, Solaris, Mirror, Stalker -> censorship and conflict with Soviet authorities -> defected -> final films in Europe -> Sculpting in Time
careerModel.keyDecision: Refused to compromise his artistic vision despite Soviet censorship, accepting exile rather than artistic compromise
careerModel.scaleModel: Seven films that became canonical in world cinema, each so distinctive it attracted a devoted global following
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about time: never compromise your vision for the institution, even if it costs you your country

profiles.oneLiner: Said a film was not shot from a script but carved from a lump of time, and defended the long take as a moral act.

profiles.name: Kenya Hara

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Art direction for Muji and consulting
careerModel.trajectory: Japanese graphic designer -> art director of Muji since 2002 -> Designing Design and White -> professor at Musashino Art University -> philosophy of emptiness as design principle
careerModel.keyDecision: Made 'emptiness' the central design principle for Muji, turning absence into the brand identity
careerModel.scaleModel: One design philosophy applied to a global brand, with books that explained the thinking to the world
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and care about emptiness: absence and restraint can be the most powerful brand identity

profiles.oneLiner: Designed the brand most associated with emptiness by treating white as a noun rather than a colour.

profiles.name: Kevin Lynch

careerModel.primaryRevenue: MIT professorship
careerModel.trajectory: MIT urban planner -> wrote The Image of the City (1960) -> introduced five elements of urban wayfinding -> foundation of how cities are understood and designed
careerModel.keyDecision: Introduced the five elements of the city image (paths, edges, districts, nodes, landmarks), creating a vocabulary for urban experience
careerModel.scaleModel: One foundational text that created the vocabulary urban designers use worldwide
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about how people navigate: create the vocabulary your field doesn't have yet, and it will be used for 60+ years

profiles.oneLiner: Proved that the city lived inside the heads of the people who walked through it, and gave designers a vocabulary for what they saw there.

profiles.name: Achille Castiglioni

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Design commissions and manufacturing royalties
careerModel.trajectory: Italian designer working first with brother Pier Giacomo, then alone -> Arco lamp, Mezzadro stool -> 50+ years of playful, ingenious industrial design -> 14 Compasso d'Oro awards
careerModel.keyDecision: Found design inspiration in everyday objects (a tractor seat became the Mezzadro stool), treating found objects as starting points
careerModel.scaleModel: Designs so clever and playful they stayed in production for decades, generating royalties
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you create and care about everyday things: look at common objects with fresh eyes, because the best design starts with what already exists

profiles.oneLiner: Said design required observation, and spent fifty years pointing at ordinary things his students had stopped seeing.

profiles.name: Marshall Ganz

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Harvard Kennedy School professorship and organizing training
careerModel.trajectory: Joined United Farm Workers with Chavez at 22 -> 28 years as organizer -> completed PhD and joined Harvard Kennedy School -> developed Public Narrative method -> trained Obama's 2008 organizers
careerModel.keyDecision: Left organizing after 28 years to get a PhD and codify organizing methodology at Harvard
careerModel.scaleModel: Practitioner who codified his methods into a teachable curriculum used to train organizers worldwide
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about leadership: spend decades in practice first, then codify and teach what you learned

profiles.oneLiner: Taught organisers that leadership is translating values into action by telling three stories.

profiles.name: Marshall McLuhan

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University of Toronto professorship and consulting
careerModel.trajectory: English professor -> Understanding Media -> 'The medium is the message' -> became the prophet of the electronic age -> fame faded, then internet vindicated everything he said
careerModel.keyDecision: Coined 'the medium is the message' and 'global village,' creating vocabulary the world still uses 60 years later
careerModel.scaleModel: Aphorisms and concepts that entered common language, making his ideas immortal even when his books went out of fashion
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about technology: coin the phrase that captures the change, because the right metaphor outlives any research paper

profiles.oneLiner: Argued that the shape of a medium did more to us than anything it carried, and spent a career making us see what we were swimming in.

profiles.name: Carl von Clausewitz

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Prussian military service
careerModel.trajectory: Prussian officer in Napoleonic Wars -> captured by French -> wrote On War as an unfinished treatise -> wife Marie published it posthumously -> became the foundational text of military strategy
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote On War as a comprehensive theory of warfare rather than just a memoir, making it applicable to all conflicts
careerModel.scaleModel: One unfinished book published posthumously that became required reading at every military academy in the world for 200 years
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and care about strategy: write the comprehensive theory of your field, even if you can't finish it, because the framework will outlive you

profiles.oneLiner: Wrote that war was simple in its parts and nearly impossible in practice, and named the reason friction.

profiles.name: John Gottman

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Gottman Institute workshops, therapist training certification, books
careerModel.trajectory: MIT math PhD -> clinical psychology researcher -> Love Lab at University of Washington -> Gottman Institute with wife Julie Schwartz Gottman -> global therapist certification empire
careerModel.keyDecision: Turned 20 years of academic research into a couples training methodology that therapists worldwide now certify in
careerModel.scaleModel: Academic research gave credibility, then a certification programme trained thousands of therapists to deliver the method without Gottman in the room
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about relationships: spend years building the evidence first, then create a certification that lets others deliver your method

profiles.oneLiner: Watched thousands of couples fight and discovered that contempt, not anger, kills a marriage.

profiles.name: Sue Johnson

careerModel.primaryRevenue: EFT therapist training and certification, books, workshops
careerModel.trajectory: Clinical psychology PhD at UBC -> developed EFT in the 1980s -> outcome research built credibility -> International Centre for Excellence in EFT -> Hold Me Tight workshops worldwide
careerModel.keyDecision: Published outcome studies that made EFT one of the few empirically validated couples therapy models, giving it an evidence edge over competitors
careerModel.scaleModel: Rigorous research created institutional trust, then a book (Hold Me Tight) and structured workshops let the method spread through both professional and consumer channels
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and care about evidence: build the outcome data first, then write the book that translates the clinical method for ordinary people

profiles.oneLiner: Showed therapists that the couple fighting about dishes is really fighting about being there.

profiles.name: Harville Hendrix

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Books, Imago therapist training certification, workshops
careerModel.trajectory: Pastoral counsellor -> divorced -> developed Imago theory from personal failure -> Getting the Love You Want -> 18 appearances on Oprah -> global Imago training network
careerModel.keyDecision: Used Oprah as the distribution channel that turned a niche therapy into a household name
careerModel.scaleModel: One bestselling book plus massive media exposure created demand, then a certification programme met it by training therapists worldwide
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and tell stories: your biggest failure might be the research question that produces your life's work, and one media hit can create a decade of demand

profiles.oneLiner: Proved that the person who drives you crazy is the exact person your psyche picked for the job.

profiles.name: Terry Real

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Relational Life Institute training, books, clinical practice
careerModel.trajectory: Family therapy training -> I Don't Want to Talk About It (1997) named male depression -> built Relational Life Institute -> became go-to voice on men and relationships
careerModel.keyDecision: Positioned himself as the therapist willing to confront men directly in session, creating a distinctive brand in a field that defaults to neutrality
careerModel.scaleModel: Provocative clinical style made for compelling training videos and books, building demand for a training institute that teaches the method to other therapists
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and speak up: being willing to say the uncomfortable thing in the room can become your entire brand, if you back it with genuine skill

profiles.oneLiner: Told men the truth about what patriarchy costs them personally, not just the women around them.

profiles.name: Gary Chapman

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Books, speaking, online quiz traffic
careerModel.trajectory: Baptist pastor in Winston-Salem -> decades of Saturday counselling -> The Five Love Languages (1992) sold slowly then exploded -> 20+ million copies -> adapted for children, teens, military, workplace
careerModel.keyDecision: Created a framework simple enough to spread without the book, with a free online quiz that kept driving new readers back to the source material
careerModel.scaleModel: One hyper-simple framework with a free assessment tool that went viral through word of mouth, spawning dozens of derivative editions for different audiences
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about relationships: make the framework so simple that people can explain it to a friend in 30 seconds, then let the quiz do the marketing

profiles.oneLiner: Gave millions of couples a shared vocabulary for why they keep missing each other.

profiles.name: Stan Tatkin

careerModel.primaryRevenue: PACT therapist training and certification, books
careerModel.trajectory: Clinical training at UCLA -> developed PACT model combining attachment and neuroscience -> Wired for Love (2012) -> PACT Institute trains therapists internationally
careerModel.keyDecision: Blended neuroscience with attachment theory to create a method that therapists could learn through body-reading skills, not just talk therapy techniques
careerModel.scaleModel: A clinically distinctive method (reading physiology, not just words) created a training programme that felt genuinely different from competing certifications
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and care about the body: combine two fields that don't usually talk to each other, and the synthesis becomes your competitive advantage

profiles.oneLiner: Taught couples that their bodies are already in the argument before their mouths open.

profiles.name: Alain de Botton

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Books, The School of Life locations, YouTube ad revenue, branded products
careerModel.trajectory: Essays on How Proust Can Change Your Life (1997) -> bestselling philosophy books -> founded The School of Life (2008) -> YouTube channel became primary distribution -> global School of Life network
careerModel.keyDecision: Opened a physical school for emotional intelligence, then pivoted to YouTube as the primary channel when the audience outgrew the shopfront
careerModel.scaleModel: Free YouTube content (8M subscribers) drives awareness, physical locations and products capture revenue, books provide credibility
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you tell stories and teach: start with the book, build the institution, then let free content on YouTube become your biggest classroom

profiles.oneLiner: Built a global school for the emotions that philosophy departments forgot to teach.

profiles.name: Gabor Mate

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Books, speaking, documentary collaborations, online courses
careerModel.trajectory: Family physician in East Vancouver -> staff physician at Portland Hotel (harm reduction) -> In the Realm of Hungry Ghosts (2008) -> global speaking career -> The Myth of Normal (2022) #1 NYT bestseller
careerModel.keyDecision: Stayed on the Downtown Eastside for 12 years treating the most severely addicted patients, building an authority that no academic researcher could match
careerModel.scaleModel: Clinical frontline experience gave moral authority, books gave reach, speaking gave revenue, each reinforcing the others
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you coach and tell stories: the years you spend in the hardest rooms build an authority that nothing else can replicate, and the books write themselves from what you witnessed

profiles.oneLiner: Said the question is never 'Why the addiction?' but always 'Why the pain?'

profiles.name: Johann Hari

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Books, speaking, TED talks
careerModel.trajectory: Newspaper columnist (The Independent) -> plagiarism scandal and public disgrace -> three years researching Chasing the Scream -> TED talk (20M+ views) -> Lost Connections -> Stolen Focus
careerModel.keyDecision: After his journalism career was destroyed by scandal, invested three years travelling to nine countries for a single book, rebuilding credibility through depth rather than speed
careerModel.scaleModel: One TED talk distilled the book's core argument ('the opposite of addiction is connection') into a sentence that travelled further than the book itself
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you tell stories and speak up: one sentence that captures a genuine insight can reach further than a career of columns, especially if you earned it by going to the places nobody else went

profiles.oneLiner: Told a world obsessed with chemical hooks that the real hook is loneliness.

profiles.name: Maia Szalavitz

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Books, journalism assignments, speaking
careerModel.trajectory: Columbia student injecting cocaine and heroin -> arrest -> recovery -> science journalism -> Help at Any Cost (2006) exposed abusive treatment industry -> Unbroken Brain (2016) reframed addiction as learning disorder
careerModel.keyDecision: Used her own addiction history not for memoir but as an epistemological tool, claiming she knows when the research is wrong because the experience does not match
careerModel.scaleModel: Rigorous science journalism with personal authority created a niche: the writer who could read the papers AND had the needle marks to challenge them
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you tell stories and speak up: your worst experience might be the credential that gives your reporting an authority no degree can match

profiles.oneLiner: Used her own needle marks as credentials to demand that addiction science stop lying to itself.

profiles.name: Carl Hart

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University salary, books, speaking
careerModel.trajectory: Grew up in poverty in Miami -> entered neuroscience to prove drug-war narrative -> PhD research contradicted own beliefs -> tenured Columbia professor -> Drug Use for Grown-Ups (2021) disclosed own heroin use
careerModel.keyDecision: Published findings that contradicted the dominant addiction narrative despite professional risk, then disclosed personal drug use to force the conversation further
careerModel.scaleModel: Tenure provided a platform safe enough to say what others could not, and personal disclosure made the academic argument impossible to ignore
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and speak up: build the institutional safety net first (tenure), then use it to say the thing everyone is afraid to say

profiles.oneLiner: Gave people drugs in a lab, measured what happened, and told the world most of what it believes about addiction is wrong.

profiles.name: Holly Whitaker

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Online recovery programme subscriptions, book
careerModel.trajectory: Director at health startup -> addiction crisis -> tried AA, found it alienating -> researched alternatives -> launched Hip Sobriety School (2014) -> rebranded to Tempest -> Quit Like a Woman bestseller (2019) -> Tempest closed (2022)
careerModel.keyDecision: Positioned sobriety as feminist empowerment rather than shame-based confession, creating a brand identity that resonated with women who would never go to AA
careerModel.scaleModel: Blog built audience, online programme captured revenue, book created mass awareness. The model worked for growth but not for financial sustainability
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you build and tell stories: reframing an old problem with a new identity (sobriety as feminism, not failure) can create explosive growth, but the business model needs to be as strong as the story

profiles.oneLiner: Asked why a programme designed by men in 1935 was still the only option for recovery.

profiles.name: Russell Brand

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Books, podcast, speaking, entertainment career
careerModel.trajectory: Heroin and crack addiction -> comedy circuit -> MTV/film career -> publicly sober -> My Booky Wook memoir -> Recovery (2017) rewrote 12 steps -> UK parliamentary testimony -> YouTube/podcast
careerModel.keyDecision: Used celebrity visibility to make recovery seem exciting and countercultural rather than defeated and shameful
careerModel.scaleModel: Entertainment career provided the megaphone, authenticity of lived experience provided the credibility, and the 12-step rewrite provided a product others could use
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and tell stories: the platform you built for entertainment can become the distribution channel for advocacy, if the personal story is real enough to survive scrutiny

profiles.oneLiner: Took the language of the rooms to the biggest stages in the world and made recovery look like something other than defeat.

profiles.name: Bill Wilson

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties (Big Book), speaking (declined salary from AA)
careerModel.trajectory: Failed stockbroker -> chronic alcoholism -> hospital spiritual experience (1934) -> met Dr. Bob Smith in Akron (1935) -> co-founded AA -> wrote Big Book (1939) -> built global movement -> died 1971
careerModel.keyDecision: Built anonymity and anti-personality principles into AA's structure, ensuring the movement could not be owned, marketed, or corrupted by any individual's ego
careerModel.scaleModel: Peer-to-peer mutual aid with zero marketing budget, no paid staff at the group level, and a book as the only product. The structure is the scale model: anyone can start a meeting, anywhere, for free
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect people and lead: the most scalable thing you can build might be the one you remove yourself from, letting the structure replicate without needing you

profiles.oneLiner: Discovered that one drunk talking to another was more powerful than any doctor or preacher.

profiles.name: Louise Aronson

careerModel.primaryRevenue: University salary (UCSF), books, speaking
careerModel.trajectory: UCSF geriatrician -> narrative medicine teacher -> Elderhood (2019) Pulitzer finalist -> became public voice for geriatric medicine reform
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote Elderhood as a hybrid of patient stories, medical evidence, and personal memoir rather than a policy book, making aging feel personal rather than statistical
careerModel.scaleModel: Academic position gave credibility and security, a trade book gave reach, and the Pulitzer nomination gave media access to argue for systemic change
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you tell stories and teach: weaving patient narratives into medical argument makes people feel what data alone cannot convey

profiles.oneLiner: Told medicine that treating old age as a disease is the disease.

profiles.name: Bill Thomas

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Consulting, Green House Project licensing, speaking, books
careerModel.trajectory: Rural geriatrician in New York -> Eden Alternative at Chase Memorial (1991) -> Green House Project (2003, Robert Wood Johnson Foundation) -> Age of Disruption tour -> elder care thought leader
careerModel.keyDecision: Moved from animals-in-nursing-homes to redesigning the nursing home itself, replacing 100-bed institutions with 10-person Green Houses
careerModel.scaleModel: Pilot project proved the concept, foundation funding scaled it, licensing let others build it, and a theatrical tour made the public case
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you design and lead: start with the smallest possible proof that your redesign works (dogs in one nursing home), then let the data justify rebuilding the entire model

profiles.oneLiner: Put dogs, cats, birds, and children into a nursing home and watched the death rate drop.

profiles.name: Ai-jen Poo

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Non-profit salary, grants, speaking, books
careerModel.trajectory: Community organiser -> co-founded Domestic Workers United -> won NY Bill of Rights (2010) -> co-founded National Domestic Workers Alliance (2007) -> MacArthur Fellow -> The Age of Dignity (2015) -> Caring Across Generations campaign
careerModel.keyDecision: Connected domestic workers' rights to the aging crisis, making the cause relevant to every family with aging parents, not just the immigrant workforce
careerModel.scaleModel: Organised isolated workers through community networks, passed state-level legislation as proof of concept, then went national. The aging angle gave the cause bipartisan appeal
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and connect: link the fight of the people nobody sees to the problem everyone fears, and the coalition builds itself

profiles.oneLiner: Organised the workforce that America depends on but refuses to protect: the women who care for our parents.

profiles.name: Marc Freedman

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Non-profit grants, books, speaking, Purpose Prize partnerships
careerModel.trajectory: Social sector background -> developed Experience Corps with AARP -> founded Civic Ventures (later Encore.org, now CoGenerate) -> Purpose Prize -> How to Live Forever (2018) -> rebranded around intergenerational connection
careerModel.keyDecision: Reframed 'retirement' as the wrong frame entirely, replacing it with 'encore' to signal that the second act could be as significant as the first
careerModel.scaleModel: Built programmes (Experience Corps) that produced research, used research to drive policy, used prizes (Purpose Prize) to create media narratives, used books to shape public imagination
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and connect: sometimes the most powerful thing you can do is give a nameless experience a name that people want to claim

profiles.oneLiner: Asked what would happen if we deployed our most experienced people instead of warehousing them.

profiles.name: Judith Heumann
