careerModel.primaryRevenue: Government positions, non-profit leadership, books, speaking, documentary
careerModel.trajectory: Denied teaching licence at 22 -> sued and won -> founded Disabled in Action -> led Section 504 sit-in (1977) -> Assistant Secretary under Clinton -> World Bank Disability Advisor -> Crip Camp (2020) Oscar nomination -> Being Heumann memoir
careerModel.keyDecision: Moved from street activism to government positions, using insider power to change policies she had once protested against from the outside
careerModel.scaleModel: Direct action created public pressure, government roles created policy change, a memoir and documentary created cultural memory. Each phase built on the last
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and lead: the same fight can be fought from the outside and then from the inside, and doing both in sequence is more powerful than either alone

profiles.oneLiner: Told a world that saw wheelchairs as tragedies that the real tragedy was the stairs.

profiles.name: Stella Young

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Journalism, ABC editorial role, speaking, comedy
careerModel.trajectory: Grew up with osteogenesis imperfecta -> studied journalism -> disability rights activism -> comedy -> edited ABC's Ramp Up -> TEDxSydney talk (10M+ views) -> died at 32
careerModel.keyDecision: Used comedy and media platforms instead of traditional advocacy channels, reaching audiences who had never thought about disability politics
careerModel.scaleModel: One TED talk ('I'm Not Your Inspiration, Thank You Very Much') became a permanent cultural reference point, and a media platform (Ramp Up) centred disabled writers
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and perform: making people laugh while telling them an uncomfortable truth gets past defences that earnest advocacy cannot

profiles.oneLiner: Told the world that being disabled does not make you brave, and that calling it brave is the problem.

profiles.name: Haben Girma

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Speaking, legal practice, books, consulting
careerModel.trajectory: Deafblind from childhood -> Harvard Law (2013) -> digital accessibility litigation -> Obama White House Champion of Change -> Haben memoir (2019) -> corporate and conference speaking
careerModel.keyDecision: Positioned accessibility as a design problem (inclusive design is cheaper than retrofitting), making the business case alongside the moral one
careerModel.scaleModel: Harvard credential opened doors, legal cases set precedents, the memoir humanised the argument, and corporate consulting provided revenue while advancing the cause
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you speak up and teach: framing a rights issue as a design problem makes it solvable, and making the business case alongside the moral case gets you into rooms that moral arguments alone cannot open

profiles.oneLiner: Graduated from Harvard Law without hearing or seeing the lectures, then turned around and sued the institutions that made it harder than it needed to be.

profiles.name: Ed Roberts

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Government salary, non-profit leadership, advocacy
revenueStreams: government salary (Director of CA Dept of Rehabilitation)
careerModel.trajectory: Paralysed by polio at 14 -> lived in iron lung -> fought into UC Berkeley (1962) -> Rolling Quads -> founded Centre for Independent Living (1972) -> appointed Director of CA Dept of Rehabilitation by Gov. Brown (1975)
careerModel.keyDecision: Built the independent living model on the principle that disabled people are the experts on their own lives, rejecting the medical model's assumption that professionals know best
careerModel.scaleModel: One centre in Berkeley became a replicable template: within a decade, 400+ independent living centres opened across the US, all following the CIL model
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and speak up: build the first one so well that others can copy it without asking permission, and the movement scales itself

profiles.oneLiner: Lived in an iron lung and still became the person who redesigned how an entire country thinks about disability.

profiles.name: Alice Wong

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Books, grants, speaking, partnerships
careerModel.trajectory: Growing up Chinese American and disabled -> launched Disability Visibility Project with StoryCorps (2014) -> anthology bestseller (2020) -> Year of the Tiger memoir (2022) -> cultural voice for disability politics
careerModel.keyDecision: Partnered with StoryCorps to give first-person disability stories a permanent home at the Library of Congress, creating infrastructure rather than just content
careerModel.scaleModel: A StoryCorps partnership built the archive, an anthology curated the best voices, a memoir personalised the politics, and Twitter became the daily distribution channel
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you connect and tell stories: sometimes the most powerful act is not telling your own story but building the platform where a community tells theirs

profiles.oneLiner: Built a megaphone for the stories that the disability rights movement had always told but that the mainstream had always ignored.

profiles.name: Muhammad Yunus

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Grameen Bank operations (interest on microloans), speaking, books, Nobel Prize
careerModel.trajectory: Economics professor at Chittagong -> $27 personal loan to 42 women (1976) -> Grameen Bank Project (1976) -> formal bank charter (1983) -> $30B+ in loans -> Nobel Peace Prize (2006) -> social business concept
careerModel.keyDecision: Made borrowers the owners of the bank (97% women), aligning incentives so that growth served the poor rather than extracting from them
careerModel.scaleModel: Group lending (five-member guarantee circles) eliminated the need for collateral, making the model replicable anywhere there was poverty and trust. Replicated in 100+ countries
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and teach: the simplest financial innovation (lending $27 with no collateral) can become the most scalable if the ownership structure protects the mission

profiles.oneLiner: Lent $27 to a village and proved that poor people pay back loans more reliably than rich ones.

profiles.name: Tiffany Aliche

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Books, courses, Live Richer Challenge, speaking
careerModel.trajectory: Preschool teacher earning $39K -> lost savings to financial fraud in 2008 -> laid off -> started The Budgetnista blog -> Live Richer Challenge (60K first cohort, 1M+ total) -> Get Good with Money NYT bestseller (2021)
careerModel.keyDecision: Made the Live Richer Challenge free and social-media-native, building an audience of over a million before monetising with a book and paid courses
careerModel.scaleModel: Free challenge built trust and audience, social media created community, book captured mainstream credibility, paid courses captured revenue. The editorial rule ('if my mother wouldn't understand it, rewrite it') kept the language accessible
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you teach and connect: give away the most valuable thing for free first, build the community around it, and the community will buy whatever you make next because they already trust you

profiles.oneLiner: Lost everything in 2008 and turned the wreckage into financial education for overlooked women.

profiles.name: Jose Quinonez

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Mission Asset Fund grants, lending circle programme fees, consulting
careerModel.trajectory: Undocumented immigrant at age 9 -> UC Davis -> Princeton master's -> founded Mission Asset Fund (2007) -> Lending Circles programme (2008) -> MacArthur Fellow (2016) -> national model for financial inclusion
careerModel.keyDecision: Did not invent lending circles but had the insight to report payments to credit bureaus, making invisible financial behaviour visible to the formal system
careerModel.scaleModel: One local programme in San Francisco's Mission District proved the concept, the MacArthur Fellowship gave national visibility, and the model was simple enough for other non-profits to replicate
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you lead and connect: the most powerful innovation is sometimes not building something new but making something that already works visible to the system that ignores it

profiles.oneLiner: Did not invent lending circles. He just made the credit bureaus notice they existed.

profiles.name: Suze Orman

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Books, TV show, speaking, financial products
careerModel.trajectory: Waitress at Buttercup Bakery for 7 years -> lost savings to Merrill Lynch broker -> sued and won -> became financial advisor -> first book (1995) -> Oprah appearances -> The Suze Orman Show on CNBC (2002-2015) -> Women and Money (2007)
careerModel.keyDecision: Treated money as an emotional subject rather than a mathematical one, making financial advice feel like therapy rather than accounting
careerModel.scaleModel: Oprah provided the initial distribution, CNBC provided weekly access to millions, books provided depth, and the confrontational 'Can I Afford It?' format created appointment television
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and teach: treating a 'boring' subject as emotionally urgent creates an audience that bland experts can never reach

profiles.oneLiner: Told millions of Americans they could not afford the life they were pretending to live, and they kept tuning in because she said it like she cared.

profiles.name: Dave Ramsey

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Books, Financial Peace University course, radio show, referral network
careerModel.trajectory: Built $4M real estate portfolio on debt -> bankrupt at 26 -> local radio show in Nashville (1992) -> Financial Peace University (1994) -> grew to 1,000+ employees, 18M weekly listeners, 10M+ FPU graduates
careerModel.keyDecision: Distributed Financial Peace University through churches, using pre-built community and accountability structures that online courses lack
careerModel.scaleModel: Free radio/podcast content builds trust, church-based course distribution provides community and accountability, referral network monetises the trust. Never accepted advertising, funding everything through product sales
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and lead: distributing your programme through existing communities (churches, workplaces) gives you accountability infrastructure that no app can replicate

profiles.oneLiner: Went bankrupt, clawed back, and spent 30 years screaming at Americans to cut up their credit cards.

profiles.name: Brené Brown
profiles.oneLiner: Turned the thing everyone hides from into the thing everyone needs.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Licensed facilitator training and corporate workshops
careerModel.trajectory: Academic researcher for 15 years, viral TED talk at 45, NYT bestselling author, Netflix special, facilitator certification empire by 55.
careerModel.keyDecision: Chose to make academic research accessible to general audiences rather than staying in the ivory tower.
careerModel.scaleModel: Licensed 300+ certified facilitators to deliver her methodology inside organisations worldwide.
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If your research makes people feel seen, package the transformation into a certified training others can deliver. You become the IP holder, not the bottleneck.

profiles.name: Tony Robbins
profiles.oneLiner: Built a cathedral of transformation you walk through in four days and leave different.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: High-ticket live transformation events
careerModel.trajectory: Running NLP seminars by 20, infomercial star by 28, arena-scale events by 30, diversified into a $7 billion portfolio by 55.
careerModel.keyDecision: Chose live events over one-on-one coaching, betting that transformation at scale would compound into a movement.
careerModel.scaleModel: Industrialised the peak experience into a repeatable 4-day container running multiple times per year across three continents.
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If you perform and coach: design one transformative container, make it repeatable, and let the live energy itself be the product.

profiles.name: Marie Forleo
profiles.oneLiner: Made business school feel like a conversation with your funniest, smartest friend.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Annual B-School enrollment (8-figure launch, once per year)
careerModel.trajectory: Bartender and fitness trainer at 23, started coaching at 25, launched MarieTV at 34, B-School at 35, NYT bestseller at 44.
careerModel.keyDecision: Limited B-School enrollment to once per year, choosing scarcity and launch energy over always-open access.
careerModel.scaleModel: Free weekly content builds trust for 50 weeks, then a 2-week annual launch converts into cohort enrollment.
careerModel.lessonsForUser: Give generously for free through one consistent content channel, then open one premium offer annually. The constraint creates event energy.

profiles.name: Wim Hof
profiles.oneLiner: Proved that a freezing river can teach you more about yourself than ten years of therapy.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Instructor certification and branded retreats
careerModel.trajectory: Grieving father using cold as medicine at 36, broke first world record at 40, academic validation at 55, 1500+ certified instructors by 64.
careerModel.keyDecision: Submitted himself to rigorous scientific testing, trading spectacle credibility for peer-reviewed credibility.
careerModel.scaleModel: Personal world records built fame, science built trust, then certified instructors delivered worldwide without him present.
careerModel.lessonsForUser: If your method works on your body first: get scientific validation, then certify others to teach it. The science turns personal practice into scalable business.

profiles.name: Adriene Mishler
profiles.oneLiner: Made the yoga mat feel like the safest place in your house.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Membership platform (FWFG) and YouTube ad revenue
careerModel.trajectory: Actress and yoga teacher at 28, first YouTube video in 2012, 30 Days of Yoga breakthrough at 30, 12M subscribers by 38, all from her living room.
careerModel.keyDecision: Kept yoga free on YouTube and optimised for accessibility over exclusivity.
careerModel.scaleModel: Free daily content builds massive trust, annual January challenges create cohort energy, low-cost membership captures the most engaged fraction.
careerModel.lessonsForUser: Be radically consistent, optimise for the person who feels too intimidated to start, and let free volume build the trust that converts into recurring revenue.

profiles.name: James Clear
profiles.oneLiner: Made the boring act of showing up every day feel like the most powerful thing you could do.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and high-fee keynote speaking
careerModel.trajectory: Photography entrepreneur in his 20s, started writing about habits at 26, built a 2M email list by 32, 20M copies sold by 38, deliberately kept the business tiny.
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote free articles twice weekly for six years before publishing a book, building the audience before the product.
careerModel.scaleModel: One book that sells itself through word of mouth, a massive newsletter, and selective high-fee speaking.
careerModel.lessonsForUser: Publish freely and consistently for years, let the audience tell you what your book should be, then keep the business radically simple.

profiles.name: Esther Perel
profiles.oneLiner: Made the mess of relationships into something you could finally talk about without shame.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Podcast, live events, and therapist training platform
careerModel.trajectory: Private practice therapist for 20 years, first book at 48, viral TED talks at 55, podcast launch at 59, training platform at 64.
careerModel.keyDecision: Made private therapy sessions public through podcast, breaking the profession's unspoken rule.
careerModel.scaleModel: Deep expertise from decades of practice, then multiple formats (audio, live, training, product) serving different engagement depths.
careerModel.lessonsForUser: Record the work (with permission), let people witness transformation, then train others in your methodology. The witnessing is the product.

profiles.name: Priya Parker
profiles.oneLiner: Proved that how you gather people is itself an act of leadership.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: High-fee facilitation for organisations and private clients
careerModel.trajectory: Conflict facilitator at 24, founded Thrive Labs, worked with WEF and MoMA, published The Art of Gathering at 38.
careerModel.keyDecision: Wrote a book codifying her facilitation principles for everyone, not just elite clients.
careerModel.scaleModel: High-fee private facilitation funds the work, the book democratises the method, workshops spread the ideas.
careerModel.lessonsForUser: Codify your invisible principles into a book or framework, then charge premium fees for live facilitation while the book builds your reputation.

profiles.name: Jay Shetty
profiles.oneLiner: Translated ancient monastic wisdom into content a scrolling generation would actually stop for.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Coaching certification school and podcast revenue
careerModel.trajectory: Monk at 23, corporate job at 26, viral video creator at 29, 4 billion views by 31, NYT bestseller at 33, coaching school by 35.
careerModel.keyDecision: Left the monastery to translate wisdom for a mass audience rather than teaching a select few.
careerModel.scaleModel: Free short-form content builds massive audience, podcast deepens trust, certification captures people who want to teach the methodology.
careerModel.lessonsForUser: Build audience with free short-form wisdom first, go deep with long-form, then certify others to teach your method.

profiles.name: Elizabeth Gilbert
profiles.oneLiner: Gave permission to be creative without waiting to be good enough first.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book royalties and keynote speaking
careerModel.trajectory: Working journalist for a decade, first book at 28, Eat Pray Love at 37 (15M copies), Big Magic at 46, patron saint of creative courage.
careerModel.keyDecision: After the crushing pressure of following up a mega-bestseller, chose to write about creative courage rather than chasing another memoir hit.
careerModel.scaleModel: One massive book creates permanent cultural permission, then speaking and mentorship serve that community.
careerModel.lessonsForUser: Externalize the pressure, separate your identity from the outcome, and remember that a decade of invisible work is not wasted.

profiles.name: Simon Sinek
profiles.oneLiner: Asked one question so simple that entire companies reorganised around the answer.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Corporate consulting and keynote speaking
careerModel.trajectory: Struggling ad man at 35, TED talk went viral at 36, bestselling author at 37, consultancy serving military and Fortune 500 by 45.
careerModel.keyDecision: Chose to build a boutique consultancy rather than scale through mass certification.
careerModel.scaleModel: One viral idea becomes multiple books, books attract enterprise clients, a small team delivers high-fee consulting.
careerModel.lessonsForUser: Codify one powerful question into a framework, let a viral moment build your reputation, then serve enterprise clients at premium fees.

profiles.name: Ali Abdaal
profiles.oneLiner: Proved you could build a business bigger than your medical salary by being curious on camera.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Cohort-based courses (PTYA) and YouTube ad revenue
careerModel.trajectory: Medical student making study videos at 22, NHS doctor with a growing channel at 24, $5M course revenue at 27, quit medicine at 28, NYT bestseller at 29.
careerModel.keyDecision: Built a YouTube audience while still employed as a doctor, proving the part-time model before teaching it.
careerModel.scaleModel: Weekly YouTube videos build authority, cohort courses convert the most engaged viewers, alumni promote organically.
careerModel.lessonsForUser: Start creating content alongside your day job, let the audience grow while you have financial safety, then launch a cohort course teaching what you demonstrated.

profiles.name: Tara Brach
profiles.oneLiner: Made sitting still with your own pain feel like the bravest thing you could do.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Teacher certification programme and retreats
careerModel.trajectory: Clinical psychologist, founded meditation community at 45, first book at 50, free podcast to 200M downloads by 70, certification training thousands of teachers.
careerModel.keyDecision: Kept the weekly teachings permanently free, trusting that generosity would build a community large enough to sustain paid offerings.
careerModel.scaleModel: Free weekly content builds global community, retreats deepen practice, 2-year teacher certification creates a lineage of practitioners.
careerModel.lessonsForUser: Give freely and consistently for decades, train teachers to carry the method, and trust that depth builds the audience.

profiles.name: Glennon Doyle
profiles.oneLiner: Built a movement by saying the things mothers were not supposed to say out loud.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Book sales and live tour events
careerModel.trajectory: Recovering addict blogging from home at 33, viral post at 36, nonprofit raising $30M, Untamed (5M copies) at 44, podcast with 300M downloads by 47.
careerModel.keyDecision: Built a nonprofit alongside her personal brand, making activism inseparable from storytelling.
careerModel.scaleModel: Radical honesty builds fierce community, community funds activism, live tours create belonging, each book deepens the movement.
careerModel.lessonsForUser: Let your personal truth be the foundation, give the community a way to act on shared values, and trust that radical honesty is itself the marketing.

profiles.name: Gabby Bernstein
profiles.oneLiner: Made spirituality accessible to the woman who still drinks oat milk lattes and checks her phone.

careerModel.primaryRevenue: Spirit Junkie Masterclass and live workshops/retreats
careerModel.trajectory: Got sober at 25, living room lectures at 29, first book at 32, Oprah endorsement at 35, 10 NYT bestsellers and 5000+ certified coaches by 44.
careerModel.keyDecision: Started teaching in her living room before having any credentials, trusting that personal transformation was qualification enough.
careerModel.scaleModel: Books build mainstream credibility, live events create peak experiences, masterclass certification creates a lineage of teachers.
careerModel.lessonsForUser: Start teaching in the smallest room available, let your transformation be the curriculum, then certify others to carry it.
